CORRECTION TO 'A MUX COSTS NOTHING' — SCOPE IT, OR IT WILL BREAK isR1CS. That entry is right that Clean's Gadgets/Conditional.lean main emits ZERO operations by building selector*(ifTrue - ifFalse) + ifFalse as an EXPRESSION. IT IS ONLY FREE IF NO DOWNSTREAM ROW NEEDS THAT VALUE TO BE AFFINE. That expression is DEGREE 2, and by the one-product-per-row constraint a row admits at most ONE product, checked syntactically. CONCRETE COUNTEREXAMPLE IN OUR OWN TREE: secp256k1-fixed-base's Mux.lean:19-31 deliberately re-implements the mux to MATERIALISE its output (ProvableType.witness + size-M assertZero rows, costed (size M, size M) at Cost.lean:334), and it HAS to — FinalAdd.lean:525-532 routes both 8/8 muxes into CheapIncompleteAdd and into Canonicalize, and CheapIncompleteAdd.isR1CS_main's signature literally demands (hAx : AffineW b.A.x). Replacing them with the free expression form would put two products on one row and be REJECTED. THE DECISION PROCEDURE: a mux is free iff every consumer of its output either (a) is itself an assertZero whose OTHER operands are all affine, so the mux's single product is that row's one permitted product, or (b) re-witnesses the value anyway. Otherwise the materialisation IS the cost of making it affine and it is not removable. AUDIT THE CONSUMERS BEFORE COSTING A MUX AT ZERO.

CYCLIC (FORWARD-REFERENCING) ROWS: THE HARNESS CLAIM IS TRUE, THE MECHANISM IS CONSTRUCTIBLE TODAY, AND IT BUYS EXACTLY ZERO — CLOSED BY AN EXHAUSTIVE EQUALITY OF TWO FAMILIES, NOT BY A FAILED SEARCH. SOURCE, VERIFIED: CostR1CSCanonicalSpec.lean:37-39 is `isCidentityRowAt (k) (e) := exists A B, Affine A and Affine B and e = var k - A*B` — A and B are arbitrary degree-<=1 expressions with NO index condition, so a row may reference witnesses allocated after its own pin; flatOperationsIsCid (same file 45-50) advances the pin counter only on .assert; Clean Circuit/Basic.lean:305 ComputableWitnesses restricts only witness GENERATORS, never constraint order. CONSTRUCTIBLE WITH ZERO NEW MACHINERY: the k12 record's own Round.lean already batch-allocates (witnessVector permutationBits) and only then emits rows (forEach ... assertZero (products[i] - chiProduct pre i)), so every row already has every witness of the batch in scope — pointing row i at products[j] with j > i is a one-token edit. THE DECISIVE REFORMULATION, which is what makes this an equality rather than a failed search: for a fixed row-set C the set R(C) of certifiable output functions is a LINEAR SUBSPACE of Fun(GF(2)^n, GF(2)) — if o1 and o2 are each constant on every fibre then so is o1+o2 — so a target of ANY output arity is r-realisable iff it lies in R(C) for some COMPLETE C, and CYCLIC BEATS ACYCLIC AT r ROWS IFF SOME R(C_cyclic) IS CONTAINED IN NO R(C_acyclic), where acyclic is exactly the multiplicative-complexity model. MEASURED, EXHAUSTIVE OVER THE FULL CANDIDATE SPACE, ZERO NOT-CONTAINED EVERYWHERE: n=3 r=1 (1024 candidates / 391 complete / 8 subspaces vs 8 acyclic); n=4 r=1 (4096/1303/36 vs 36); n=3 r=2 (16777216/2608285/51 vs 43); n=4 r=2 (268435456/22302253/2641 vs 2521); n=5 r=2 (4294967296/225461581/67581 vs 66341). Self-references (A or B naming the PINNED variable) AND forward references were both in the space. FREE UNPINNED WITNESSES ARE WORTH NOTHING — e = 1,2,3 give IDENTICAL subspace families. Independent z3 cross-check on a separate encoding: chi3 UNSAT at r=1 and r=2 and SAT at r=3, chi5 UNSAT at r=3 in both modes, AND5 SAT at r=4 = MC. THE ONE SCALE-FREE CONSEQUENCE: the r-certifiable class is closed under substituting constants for inputs, and ANF degree is detected by restriction, so the exhaustive finding that NO degree-4 function on 4 variables is 2-row certifiable (measured degree histograms: r=1 -> max degree 2, r=2 -> max degree 3, reconfirmed over all 67581 subspaces at n=5) gives deg f <= r+1 for r <= 2 IN ANY NUMBER OF VARIABLES — exactly Schnorr's DETERMINISTIC bound MC(f) >= deg(f) - 1. So the purest composition z = f(g(x)) with g = (x0x1, x2x3) and f = uv, i.e. AND4 with MC = 3, is NOT certifiable by 2 cyclic rows, exhausted over all 268435456 two-row systems. CONJECTURED for all r, with a partial proof: normalise row 1 to w1*B' = C' with B',C' free of w1 (over GF(2), w1(b + beta*w1) = c + gamma*w1 iff w1(b + beta + gamma) = c); if B' contains no witness the split B'=0 / B'=1 is an INPUT hyperplane and each half eliminates row 1, so f has degree <= r on each half and <= r+1 globally. THE GAP: when B' contains other witnesses the split is not an input predicate and the covering sets need not be affine. STILL OPEN AND WHAT IT COSTS: r >= 3 is TIMED OUT, NOT EMPTY — the r=3 degree probe died at 5400s, AND5@r=3 and AND6@r=4 at 3600s, chi5@r=4 at 1800s; the cheap close is an exhaustive C search at n=3 r=3, about 5 CPU-hours. Toy scale also cannot see the width x depth question at all: 2 rounds of a 3-bit permutation IS a 3-bit permutation and both models reach it at r=2. DO NOT SPEND JOB SLOTS ON CYCLIC GF(2) ROW SETS. Re-open ONLY on a refutation of deg <= r+1 at r >= 3, or an explicit row-set at any size whose R(C) is in no acyclic R(C') of the same row count. NOTE WHICH DIRECTION IS LIVE: cyclicity is an UPPER-BOUND tool, so only a CONSTRUCTION can close it — no lower bound can help, since our own ceiling theorem says no counting/rank/degree argument separates k12's 19200 from 1600, and no explicit n-variable function is known to have MC > n-1.

SCOPE CORRECTION — FORWARD REFERENCES ARE A NEW DEGREE OF FREEDOM ONLY IN THE TWO GF(2) CHALLENGES, AND THE FIVE R1CS CHALLENGES ALREADY HAVE A STRICTLY STRONGER NON-MATERIALISING PRIMITIVE. In model A the row predicate is `isR1CSRow e := match r1csProducts e with | some k => k <= 1 | none => False` (Challenge/Utils/CostR1CS.lean:79-82) — PURELY SYNTACTIC on the expression, it never mentions a variable index, and flatOperationsIsR1CS carries no counter. So (i) forward references were NEVER restricted there, and (ii) model A additionally admits rows with NO FRESH WITNESS AT ALL — a pure assertion A*B = C — which the C-identity form forbids, since every GF(2) row must introduce and pin a new variable. EVERY MODULAR-REDUCTION CERTIFICATE IN THE SECP AND RSA RECORDS IS A NON-MATERIALISING VERIFICATION OF EXACTLY THAT KIND — MulModEqFold is the purest example, asserting a*b = s1+s2 mod p with no remainder witnessed at all. So 'can a rank-one system verify a composition without materialising the intermediates' IS NOT AN UNEXPLOITED IDEA IN MODEL A; IT IS THE STANDARD TECHNIQUE, and the live lever there is range-bit accounting of the values that ARE witnessed, not cyclicity. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE 'SAME OPEN GAP' ENTRY: identifying (a) the RSA joint certificate, (b) the k12 non-affine round output and (c) the secp master cost law as ONE question is right as slogan and WRONG AS MECHANISM — (b) lives in a strictly weaker row model than (a) and (c). The GF(2) negative CLOSES (b) and closes the cyclic-row mechanism corpus-wide; it does NOT close (a) or (c). SECOND CORRECTION, TO (b)'s PHRASING: 'can a round's output be NOT affine in (x,w) while the next round's AND multiplicands are still affine forms' is close to a CATEGORY ERROR — in the C-identity model every multiplicand is an affine FORM in (x,w) by fiat, there is no syntactic slot for a non-affine intermediate, and the only content is how many pinned witnesses the affine span must contain, which is exactly the row count. That is WHY the exhaustive search found nothing: cyclicity adds no mechanism, it only widens which affine forms a row may multiply, and the R(C)-subspace test enumerates all of those.

'ASSERTION, NOT VALUE' DELETES TARGETS, NOT OPERANDS — THE SCOPE RULE, AND IT IS WHAT DECIDES WHETHER THE MECHANISM TRANSFERS. MulModEqFold is worth -531 per site because it deletes a materialised value that is only ever the TARGET of a certificate: nothing reads it, it merely has to satisfy an equation, so the folded certificate runs directly against the target expression and the witness disappears. IT CANNOT DELETE AN OPERAND. An operand of a non-native product must have LIMB-CERTIFIED DIGITS or its F_p convolution coefficients carry no integer meaning — verified by 200/200 forgeries at toy scale on the RSA tree. SO THE AUDIT QUESTION IS NOT 'does anything read this value' BUT 'does anything read it AS AN OPERAND OF A PRODUCT'. Worked example of each: on secp256k1 the curve-equation residue in PointValid and the terminal slope residue are TARGETS, and deleting them was worth -531 each; on RSA the 15 chain residues r_i are each read as the operand a of the NEXT squaring's convolution, so all 15 are irreducible, and the single target-only node (the terminal a^2*b = q*n + em) was ALREADY folded. A THIRD CATEGORY THAT LOOKS DELETABLE AND IS NOT: a value nobody reads whose RANGE CHECK IS ITSELF THE CERTIFICATE — the RSA quotients q_i are read by no one, but removing their range checks is a forgery, not a saving, because the dimension count (171 free unknowns against 37 group equations) is what pins the reduction. CLASSIFY EVERY CANDIDATE AS TARGET / OPERAND / CERTIFICATE-BY-RANGE BEFORE COSTING IT.

OFFSETTING ONLY ONE OPERAND OF A BILINEAR CONVOLUTION SAVES EXACTLY ZERO — PROVED, AND IT KILLS A WHOLE FAMILY OF 'BALANCE THE LIMBS' IDEAS. For a bilinear convolution with per-limb cap M and offsets a,b <= M/2, writing A = M - a and B = M - b, the balanced coefficient bound is A*B + a*B + A*b = M^2 - a*b. Minimised at a = b = M/2, giving exactly 0.75*M^2, i.e. a cap gain of log2(4/3) = 0.415 BITS — not the ~1.32 a naive 'halve both operands' reading suggests. Setting b = 0 gives M^2 - 0: THE CROSS TERM COSTS BACK PRECISELY WHAT THE ONE-SIDED BALANCING SAVES. CONSEQUENCES ALREADY BANKED: on RSA this cut the q*n cap lever from a claimed 1467 to a measured 218, and zeroed a claimed ~130 for balancing b in the final block, where a is genuinely balanced (a change of the certified quantity, no cross term) and b is exactly the one-sided case. The gain is FURTHER DILUTED wherever the carry width is log2(OFF_P + OFF_N) and only one side's OFF is touched. Before costing any limb-balancing idea, check whether BOTH operands can be offset; if only one can, the answer is zero without further work.

THE CONSUMER-FUNCTIONAL LAW — THE QUANTITATIVE FORM OF 'ASSERTION, NOT VALUE'. An emulated field element used only as a CERTIFICATE ADDEND has TWO coordinates, not four. The yes/no test asks whether a value is read at all; the sharp form is PER-COORDINATE and is a rank computation. A multi-cell value costs in proportion to its NUMBER OF CELLS in every gadget that builds it by selection (mux tree, one-hot contraction, table lookup, packed-borrow select), but each consumer reads only a set of LINEAR FUNCTIONALS of the cell vector. THE NUMBER OF CELLS THAT MUST BE PRODUCED IS dim span{all consumers' functionals}, NOT the arity of the ProvableType. PROVED FROM SOURCE for the folded certificate, the dominant consumer in both secp trees: GroupedFlex.main (fixed-base GroupedFlex.lean:195-205) emits exactly two kinds of row — carryLoop ... (G-2) 0, and one final assertZero (polyEvalExpr (Pc - Sc) (2^B)). With G = 3 at every call site the carryLoop runs ONE iteration, range-checking carryExpr 0, which reads positions posOf 0 .. posOf 0 + gf 0 - 1; with gfFold = 2 and posOfFold k = 2k that is positions {0,1} ONLY. Positions 2,3,4 appear in NO row but the single final polyEval row, which reads sum_k coeff_k 2^(64k). SO A TARGET/ADDEND VECTOR ENTERS THROUGH EXACTLY TWO INDEPENDENT FUNCTIONALS: T_lo = t_0 + 2^64 t_1 and T_hi = t_2 + 2^64 t_3. THE COMPLEMENTARY FACT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT UNIVERSAL: a value used as a MULTIPLICAND of interpolatedMul is read through 2m-1 EVALUATIONS of its limb polynomial at distinct constants, which is FULL RANK m — a multiplicand always needs all four limbs and this can never apply to one. RANK LEDGER, APPLY MECHANICALLY: convolution multiplicand -> 4; certificate addend under a one-carry group schedule -> 2; value only tested for zero or equality -> 1 (subject to the boundedness caveat in the costed-negatives entry); circuit output -> whatever the interface declares. AUDIT RULE: for every value produced by a SELECTOR, list its consumers, write down each consumer's functionals, and produce only a BASIS of their span.

'ASSERTION, NOT VALUE' AND ITS MULTIPLICAND DUAL ARE STRUCTURALLY VACUOUS IN COST MODEL B — DO NOT SWEEP gf2-sha256 OR gf2-k12 FOR EITHER; IT IS A CATEGORY ERROR. From the trusted surface, CostR1CSCanonicalSpec.lean:37-39 and 45-50: isCidentityRowAt k e := exists A B, Affine A and Affine B and e = var k - A*B, and flatOperationsIsCid advances the pin counter on EVERY assert and on no witness. Two consequences. (1) EVERY ROW MATERIALISES EXACTLY ONE VALUE BY FIAT: the C-side must be a bare variable var k, so there is no row that checks a certificate without introducing a value, and 'delete the materialisation and run the certificate against the target' has no syntactic slot to live in. Model A's non-materialising pure assertion A*B = C is FORBIDDEN here. (2) EVERY MULTIPLICAND IS ALREADY AN AFFINE FORM BY FIAT: A and B range over all degree-<=1 expressions, so 'a value consumed only as a multiplicand should be an affine form, not a witness' is already true of every multiplicand, and there is nothing to convert. The only remaining question in model B is HOW MANY rows, i.e. AND count. EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION THAT NEITHER TREE HAS A STRAY WITNESS: gf2-sha256's record declares allocations = 22215 AND constraints = 22215; gf2-k12 is 19200/19200. Allocations equal constraints to the unit in both, and since allocations >= constraints is forced there while any surplus allocation is an unpinned universally-quantified variable worth nothing, EQUALITY IS PROOF THAT NOT ONE VALUE IS MATERIALISED WITHOUT BEING PINNED AND CONSUMED. There is no dead-value sweep to run on either GF(2) slug, now or ever.

FIVE COSTED NEGATIVES AROUND THE PACKING / NON-MATERIALISATION FAMILY — ALL CHECKED, ALL EMPTY, WITH THE ARITHMETIC. (1) PACKED CONDITIONAL EQUALITY NEEDS A BOUND ON THE WITNESS SIDE AND THAT IS USUALLY THE WHOLE COST. The gadget s * (sum_i 2^((b+1)i) (u_i - v_i)) = 0 collapses k conditional equalities into ONE row (one product, zero allocations) and is sound when every residual is a signed integer below 2^b and (b+1)k < log2 p - 1. It fails wherever the pinned value is a FREE WITNESS: in sha256's SelectDigest the 8 digest words are witnessed and pinned by 5 groups x 8 rows = 8 alloc / 40 rows; packing 4 words per row would give 8/10 (-30) but the digest words carry no row-level bound, so a prover cancels 2^33*d_1 against d_0 and the pack is UNSOUND. Buying the bound costs 8 x 32 range-check bits. (2) MERGING TWO MODULAR CERTIFICATES UNDER ONE CARRY CHAIN SAVES NOTHING. Packing two integer identities E1 + 2^K E2 = 0 at disjoint bit ranges is sound (no challenge, so not Schwartz-Zippel) and worthless: each certified integer is ~2^300, the grouped carry exists precisely to cut a 300-bit identity into sub-p groups, and packing two just doubles the group count. CARRY BITS ARE PROPORTIONAL TO TOTAL IDENTITY WIDTH, WHICH IS INVARIANT. (3) THE MUX CANNOT BE PACKED BY ITS COMMON SELECTOR. sum_i B^i (w_i - b_i) = s * sum_i B^i (a_i - b_i) is genuinely ONE product once factored and would turn an m-cell mux from m alloc + m rows into m alloc + 1 row — but the w_i are free witnesses and the same unboundedness kills it. It becomes available exactly when the mux output is range-checked downstream for another reason; in both secp trees the mux-output limb bounds come from the SPEC (proof-side, free), never from rows. (4) sha256's Round0Block1Sparse is 32 alloc + 33 rows and the top-bit-free trick does NOT apply: dropping the top bit forces witnessing the wrap carry instead, 32/33 either way. (5) keccak's chi is at the dimension floor with its row already saturated, so there is no assertion-not-value site and no free product slot there.

LOWER BOUNDS STATED ONLY FOR 'QUADRATIC' OR SIGMA-PI-SIGMA CIRCUITS APPLY IN FULL FORCE TO COST MODEL B — THE USUAL CAVEAT IS NOT A CAVEAT FOR US. Much of the multiplicative-complexity literature proves bounds only for QUADRATIC CIRCUITS (every gate computes a function of degree <= 2) or SIGMA-PI-SIGMA form, and states this as a restriction that weakens the result relative to general circuits. OUR TWO GF(2) CHALLENGES ARE LITERALLY THAT CLASS: isCidentityRowAt k e := exists affine A B, e = var k - A*B makes every row a product of TWO AFFINE FORMS pinned to a fresh variable, which is exactly a quadratic / SigmaPiSigma gate. SO WHEN SCANNING THE LITERATURE FOR APPLICABLE BOUNDS, DO NOT DISCARD A RESULT BECAUSE IT IS 'ONLY' FOR QUADRATIC CIRCUITS — that is our model exactly, and such a result is STRICTLY MORE APPLICABLE here than a general-circuit bound would be elsewhere. WORKED EXAMPLE: Boyar et al., 'Multiplicative Complexity of Vector Valued Boolean Functions' (arXiv:1407.6169), Corollary 1 — 'any quadratic circuit computing an almost bent (n,n)-function has at least L(n,(n-1)/2) AND gates, and for sufficiently large n that exceeds 2.32n'. For a general circuit this would be a restricted statement; against model B it is a direct bound. The same reading applies to any ANF-degree or rank argument in that literature. NOTE THE CONVERSE, so this is not over-applied: cost model A (the five R1CS challenges) is NOT the quadratic-circuit class, because a row there may carry no fresh witness at all and the constraint system need not be a circuit in any order — see the forward-reference scope entry.

A NEW RECORD CAN SILENTLY LOSE GROUND THE PREVIOUS RECORD HELD — ALWAYS DIFF A RECORD AGAINST ITS PREDECESSOR FOR LOST ATOMS, NOT ONLY FOR GAINED ONES. THE MECHANISM: check_records reseeds projs/<slug>/Solution/ when a record moves, but jobs already in flight keep their OLD checkout ('running jobs left to finish'). A job that started before record N lands can therefore produce record N+1 that is BETTER OVERALL yet MISSING everything N added — and nothing in the loop notices, because the only test applied is 'does the total beat the leaderboard'. MEASURED INSTANCE, secp256k1-fixed-base: the 52256 record descends from the 52676 seed, not from the 52430 record that preceded it. Evidence, three independent atoms: implicitScreenedCost is 1640/1649 (the 52676 value; 52430 had 1634/1643), the three folded-quotient RangeCheck widths are 68/70/68 (the 52676 values; 52430 had shaved them to 67/69/67), and combCost 26280/26396 - 26070/26186 = 210/210 = exactly 21 x the selectCost delta 298/299 -> 288/289. So 52256 = 52676 - 420 and the 52430 record's -246 IS NOT IN IT. THE TWO ARE ORTHOGONAL AND STACK: re-applying the lost 246 to the current tree gives ABOUT 52010 for zero new ideas. GENERAL PRACTICE, now three variations on one theme: (a) when two jobs both beat the seed, diff their atoms — the loser's cheaper atoms are free score; (b) when a record lands, diff it against the PREVIOUS RECORD and re-apply any atom that got worse; (c) the cheap discriminator for whether two trees are the same work is the DECLARED allocations/constraints pair, never the tarball hash, which moves with comments and proof text. ALSO RE-CHECK ON THIS SLUG: hot4 in the 52256 tree takes `h : Var (fields 15)` where an earlier note recorded `fields 14` from two affinely-derived cells — determine whether that refinement was lost too before re-costing the one-hot item.

A FAILED VERIFICATION IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A TIMEOUT — CHECK THE DURATION AGAINST KNOWN SUCCESSES BEFORE BLAMING ELABORATION COST. Instance: sha256-hash submission bdc0ff37 claiming 145471 (-8) came back status=failed with score=None after 17.5 minutes, and the natural reading was the timeout that this corpus has previously lost a submission to. THE DURATIONS SAY OTHERWISE. Measured submitted_at -> verified_at on recent submissions: fixed-base 50825 VERIFIED in 19.2 min, secp256k1-scalar-mul 331777 VERIFIED in 12.7, 342300 VERIFIED in 12.5, rsa 321769 VERIFIED in 14.1, against the FAILED sha256 at 17.5. A SUCCESS RAN LONGER THAN THE FAILURE, so 17.5 min is nowhere near a cliff and verification duration carries NO timeout signal in the 12-20 minute band. The failure is therefore a genuine proof or soundness rejection, not an elaboration budget problem. NOTE WHAT THE API DOES AND DOES NOT GIVE: the submission record exposes status, score, allocations, constraints, description, submitted_at and verified_at, but NO failure reason and NO log — so diagnosing a rejection means re-deriving it locally from the submitted tree, BUT THE TREE IS *NOT* RETRIEVABLE FROM THE API — I ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE HERE AND IT IS WRONG. /api/submissions/<id>/download returns HTTP 409 {"detail": "Only verified submissions can be downloaded."} for BOTH failed and still-pending submissions; only a VERIFIED submission downloads (measured on all three states). SO A FAILED SUBMISSION'S TREE EXISTS IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE: the local out/<slug>/ directory the tick extracted it into — and the NEXT job on that slug overwrites it. If a failure is worth diagnosing, copy out/<slug>/ aside IMMEDIATELY on the failure notification; after the next tick it is gone for good. The description field of that submission listed several aggressive claims worth suspecting first when one does fail: 'affine carry chain: zero carry allocations', 'terminal schedule words left unreduced', and '7-of-8 bits per byte'.
sha256-hash: CALIBRATION REBUILT FROM ACTUAL CIRCUIT GENERATION (every number below was measured by building the circuit and counting, not quoted). Per ONE 512-bit compression, plain R1CS, no lookups: jsnark 25656 with the constant IV and 25968 generic (variable chaining value) — verified by emitting the real .arith and applying CircuitReader's instruction-to-R1CS mapping; xJsnark claims 25538 (paper Table III, same jsnark->libsnark pipeline, credible but not independently re-measured); bellman 25840 BUT THAT IS A CONSTANT-IV FIRST-BLOCK ARTIFACT — a generic bellman block is 26192 (26166 nonlinear), because with a constant IV the first rounds' ch/maj/rotate-XORs fold away; libsnark 27280 (NOT the widely repeated 27904, which appears in no libsnark file, test or constant and is folklore), rising to 27792 if you count input booleanity, which libsnark deliberately omits (issue #37); arkworks crypto-primitives about 40880 per block, a naive port, not a target; gnark about 25.8k marginal but OUT OF SCOPE and irrelevant anyway, since std/math/uints is built on 2^8 x 2^8 lookup tables plus about 130k fixed table cost. WATCH THE CONVENTION: these differ by whether the 512 message bits' booleanity is counted (jsnark 25392 excluding vs 25968 as measured). Pin that down before claiming a win.

CORRECTION — ONE ROW PER BIT IS NOT THE FLOOR FOR Ch AND Maj; THE RECORD IS AT HALF A ROW PER BIT. I previously wrote that we were 'already at ONE row per Maj bit including booleanity' and used that to reject jsnark's cross-round Maj sharing (which gets 1.5 multiplications per Maj bit and is indeed a regression against 1). BOTH HALVES NEED UPDATING: the jsnark trick is still a regression, but our floor is now 0.5 alloc + 0.5 constr per bit via lambda-packed twin instances (see the _common entry). CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE-CLASSIFICATION WORK: the exhaustive SMT sweep that found 192 of 256 three-input functions to be single-row NATIVE answered the question for ONE instance of a function. The open and more valuable question is WHICH PAIRS OF NATIVE FUNCTIONS SHARING INPUTS ADMIT A SINGLE LAMBDA-PACKED ROW — that is where the remaining factor of two lives, and the sweep has not been run for it.
Majority(B,C,D) = (B&C) ^ (B&D) ^ (C&D): three ANDs + XOR-fold; Ch(E,F,G) = G ^ (E&(F^G)) uses ONE AND (E&(F^G)) instead of two.

Represent each 32-bit word's bits once and reuse; XOR / rotation / shift are FREE affine combinations of bit variables — never allocate constraints for them, only for the AND (booleanity + one rank-1 product).

CALIBRATION, CORRECTED AND MEASURED (the widely-quoted numbers are wrong in two places). bkomuves/hash-circuits' 26170 is labelled 'approximate' in its own README, appears nowhere else, and ships no benchmark harness; compiled here with circom 2.2.3 --O2 it is 26232 general / 26040 constant-IV (budget: rounds 64x294 + 264 = 19080, schedule 48x149 = 7152). libsnark's real figure is 27280 (sha256_gadget.tcc: `return 27280; /* hardcoded for now */`) — THE WIDELY-CITED 27904 IS FOLKLORE, traceable to no primary source. circomlib Sha256compression() = 30328 nonlinear (--O2; 30952 at --O0), Sha256(256) = 29412, Sha256(512) = 59313. bellman = 25840, a hard CI assertion at src/gadgets/sha256.rs:331, constant-IV, so it beats bkomuves' constant-IV 26040 by 200. THE PUBLISHED FRONTIER IS xJsnark's 25538 (Kosba et al., S&P 2018, Table III; Buffet 44999 / Geppetto 38556). ALL of these count NONLINEAR CONSTRAINTS ONLY, with no allocations, so none of them is directly comparable to our allocations+constraints score — and none of them threatens it. Verified-zkEVM/clean's own public Clean/Gadgets/SHA256/ (main branch, NOT PR #395) is about 40280: chained two-operand Add32 at 33 each, written for provability rather than cost. gnark, Noir and arkworks-via-lookups are OUT OF SCOPE (LogUp / plookup / BSB22 commitments).
Carry-save (3:2 compressor) addition to combine the 6-7 addends in the round function before a single final modular reduction, rather than chained 2-input adds.

CORRECTION — THE TOP-CARRY-BIT-AS-AFFINE-COMBINATION IS ALREADY APPLIED, AND IT GOES FURTHER THAN THE -1/-1 I CLAIMED. My earlier note said no implementation defines the top carry bit affinely and that doing so saves 1 allocation + 1 constraint per decomposition. The RECORD SOLUTION ALREADY DOES IT, in three places, and beats that figure: (a) CarrySumAdd32 witnesses ONLY the 32 output bits and makes EVERY carry — including the top — affine, via the recursion c_{n+1} = 2^-1*(a[n] + b[n] + c_n - z[n]); a full 32-bit modular add is 32 allocations + 32 constraints with ZERO carry allocations AND NO TIE ROW, because each carry's DEFINITION is the sum equation. The per-bit row is (c_next + a[i] + b[i] - 9c + 3)*(a[i] + b[i] + 6c - 4) + 12 = 0. (b) The fused round adders define their BOTTOM carry bit affinely and assert only its booleanity, which discharges two packed 32-bit reductions at once. (c) Every message byte witnesses 7 bits, not 8: hi = 128^-1*(byte - sum 2^t low[t]). THE RESIDUAL QUESTION, AND IT IS CLOSED: can a SECOND carry bit per fused adder also be made affine? No — one field identity solves for exactly one unknown, so all remaining carry bits must be witnessed. GENERAL RULE THAT SURVIVES: in any decomposition, allocate k-1 of the k bits and derive the last affinely; a k-bit range check costs 2k-1, not 2k.

Smart bitwidth adjustment (xJsnark): track a STATIC upper bound on every intermediate 32-bit word through the adds/XOR-folds and insert a bit-decomposition/normalization ONLY when that bound would overflow the native field — not after every operation. Reported ~3.2k constraints saved vs Geppetto and ~10k vs Buffet on SHA-256; each skipped decomposition removes 32 allocations + its booleanity constraints, so it pays double in this metric.

Global common-subexpression / multivariate-polynomial minimization across the 64 rounds (xJsnark, reported ~8.8k constraints on SHA-256): the message schedule and round function reuse the same sigma/XOR-fold subexpressions — allocate each distinct affine combination ONCE and share it everywhere rather than per-round.

If the framework exposes lookups: 'spread'/interleaved-bit tables (Barretenberg-style) turn XOR3 and Maj into table reads; only worth it if a lookup is cheaper than the ~1 constraint the arithmetic form already costs — verify against this R1CS cost model first.

Boyar-Peralta counter bound also applies to the NATIVE SHA-256 challenge's bit-level adders: MC of Hamming weight of n bits is exactly n - H(n), so multi-operand column addition wants optimal k:log(k) counters, not chained 3:2 compressors. Weigh against the field-arithmetic route here (a native field can add many 32-bit words in one linear combination and range-check once) — pick whichever costs fewer allocations+constraints, but do not assume chained full adders are optimal.

CORRECTION — 184 DECOMPOSITIONS PER BLOCK IS NOT THE FLOOR; THE RECORD DOES 180. My earlier note called 184 the 'settled' design (64x2 rounds + 48 schedule + 8 final) and said anything above it was free score. The record measures 180: 128 for the rounds (64x2, unchanged), **46** schedule words instead of 48, and **6** final chaining adds instead of 8. The two structural reasons are separate entries below — w62/w63 are never reduced or decomposed because nothing downstream reads their BITS, and the chaining adds for state words 0 and 4 are folded into round 63's own reduction. THE SHARING CLAUSES OF THE ORIGINAL NOTE ARE ALL CORRECT AND ARE HONOURED BY THE RECORD: d and h are never FRESHLY decomposed (they exist as bit vectors only because they are earlier a's and e's), b/c are previous a's, f/g previous e's, a's bits serve Sigma0 and Maj, e's bits serve Sigma1 and Ch, rotations are re-indexing. circomlib's 4-per-round remains the outlier. TREAT 180 AS THE NUMBER TO BEAT, and ask of every remaining decomposition whether ANY consumer reads an individual bit.

THE PREMISE THAT MODULAR REDUCTION DOMINATES THE NATIVE COST IS FALSE — BIT-LOGIC IS THE COST, AND MY EARLIER PROJECTION OF WHAT A GOLFED BLOCK COSTS WAS 17% PESSIMISTIC. Corrected against the record's own cost proofs, for one GENERIC 512-bit block: rounds 21062 (31 round-pairs at 658 plus a 664 tail pair), schedule 8627 (23 step-pairs at 365 plus two 58/58 last steps), final chaining adds 384 — TOTAL 30073 score per block. I had projected about 35.1k (25216 + 9360 + 520); all three sub-budgets are beaten, the rounds budget by 4154. Where the round cost actually sits, per PAIR of rounds (328 alloc / 330 constr): four upper sigmas 128, four 32-bit word decompositions 128 allocations + 128 booleanity, packed Ch 32/32, packed Maj 32/32, and the two fused adders 8 allocations + 10 constraints for FOUR 32-bit modular reductions. So the reductions are about 3% of a round pair and the bit-logic and decompositions are the rest. Block 0 (constant IV) is 29780 and the final padding-only block is 21442 because its whole schedule is affine.

BLOCK 0's CHAINING VALUE IS THE CONSTANT IV — this challenge hashes a MESSAGE, not a compression with a variable state, so every operation consuming the initial state in block 0 is against compile-time constants and is partially foldable. In the Boolean world that alone is worth -301 ANDs (Goldfeder's sha256Unpadded.txt = 22272 vs Bristol's general 22573; github.com/matteocam/sha256-circuit). In the native world it is the difference between bkomuves' 26232 and 26040. Make sure the first block is specialized and not calling the same generic compression circuit as blocks 1..n.

CLOSED — bellman's MultiEq IS ENTIRELY SUBSUMED, AS SUSPECTED. The open question was whether the framework charges for standalone affine equality (tie) rows, in which case bellman's trick of packing ~7 sum-equalities into one row by bit-offsetting them would pay. IT DOES NOT ARISE: the record has NO TIE ROWS ANYWHERE, because every carry is defined as the affine expression that the sum identity solves for, so the identity is discharged by asserting the carry's booleanity and never appears as a separate row. Do not spend a slot on MultiEq.

DO-NOT-TRY, AND IT IS A TEMPTING ONE: XOR-GATE / SHORTEST-LINEAR-PROGRAM MINIMIZATION BUYS EXACTLY ZERO HERE. There is a large and still-active literature on minimizing the number of 2-input XOR gates needed to evaluate an F2-LINEAR MAP — the Shortest Linear Program problem: Boyar-Peralta, Tan-Peyrin (TCHES'20) adding randomization and 3-input XOR gates, the 'Superior Boyar-Peralta' (SBP) depth-aware heuristic, 'Improved Heuristics for Low-Latency Implementations of Linear Layers', and eprint 2025/1493 which revisits BP and cuts the AES linear layer from 91 to 89 g-XOR. Keccak's theta (and rho/pi, and SHA-256's Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1) are exactly such linear maps, so this looks like the obvious attack on the biggest remaining slack. IT IS NOT, BECAUSE AN XOR GATE COSTS NOTHING IN EITHER OF OUR COST MODELS. In native R1CS an affine combination lives inside the A/B/C vectors of a row and is free. In the GF(2) challenges the harness restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A and B AFFINE, so an arbitrary XOR-combination is free inside a multiplicand. Halving the XOR count of theta changes the score by ZERO. WHAT THETA'S 2240 ROWS PER ROUND ACTUALLY PAY FOR IS *MATERIALIZATION*, NOT XOR COUNT: a value costs an allocation exactly when it must appear as a BARE WITNESS VARIABLE — because it is a circuit output, or because its consumer needs a variable rather than an affine form. THEREFORE THE ONLY QUESTION WORTH ASKING IS: for each currently-materialized intermediate, WHO CONSUMES IT, and can that consumer take an affine form instead? Every row saved comes from deleting a materialization, never from restructuring the XOR tree that feeds it.

LAMBDA-FUSED MULTI-OPERAND MODULAR ADDITION — TWO 32-BIT REDUCTIONS FOR 5 ALLOCATIONS AND 6 CONSTRAINTS, WITH NO TIE ROW. Do not emit one 'sum = value' equality per modular reduction. Pack TWO independent 6-operand mod-2^32 reductions into ONE field identity at base lambda = 2^40 (both sums are < 2^35 so the slots cannot collide over BN254), witness all but one of the carry bits, and DEFINE the remaining carry bit as the affine expression the identity solves for. Asserting only that this expression is boolean then discharges BOTH sum equations and its own range at once. MEASURED (the E-path adder across two SHA-256 rounds): witness 2 carry bits for round t and 3 for round t+1 = 5 allocations; 5 booleanity rows plus 1 row for the derived low carry = 6 constraints. The A-path adder (5 operands, 2 carry bits per round) is 3 allocations / 4 constraints. TOTAL 8 allocations + 10 constraints for FOUR 32-bit modular reductions in a round pair. THE DERIVED CARRY: lowCarry = 2^-32*(sum operands_t + z_packed + lambda*sum operands_{t+1} - out_t - lambda*(out_{t+1} + 2^32*carry_{t+1})) - 2*c_t[1] - 4*c_t[2], then assertZero(lowCarry*(lowCarry - 1)). Note the packed Ch/Maj word enters as a SINGLE expression and splits into the two lambda-slots automatically. Subtracting a state word is not32(d) + 1 — two's complement, affine, free.

FUSE THE FINAL CHAINING ADDITION INTO THE LAST ROUND'S OWN REDUCTION. The Merkle-Damgard feed-forward H[i] += state[i] is normally 8 separate 32-bit adds after the 64 rounds. TWO OF THEM ARE FREE: round 63 already computes new_e and new_a by a modular reduction, so add the chaining value INTO THAT SAME SUM and witness the result once. MEASURED: out4 := s4 + c + g + Sigma1' + Ch + K63 + w63 and out0 := out4 + s0 - s4 + Sigma0' + Maj - c + 2, each a single 32-bit decomposition inside the round-63 gadget, so only 6 of the 8 chaining adds survive as standalone adders. SAVES 2 decompositions = 64 score per block and takes the per-block decomposition count from 182 to 180. The extra operands widen the sum by one bit, absorbed by the existing carry witnesses. GENERALISES to any Merkle-Damgard hash: any last-round output word that coincides with a feed-forward target is free to fold.

PACK THE 2-INPUT-XOR LANES OF sigma0/sigma1 — 58 WITNESSES FOR 64 SIGMA LANES, NOT 64, AND NEVER MATERIALISE THE SIGMA WORDS. SHA-256's SCHEDULE sigmas contain a SHIFT, so their top lanes degenerate to 2-input XORs: sigma0 = rotr7 ^ rotr18 ^ shr3 is a genuine 3-input XOR only on lanes 0..28, and sigma1 = rotr17 ^ rotr19 ^ shr10 only on lanes 0..21. A 3-input lane needs its own witness (single-row form), but TWO 2-INPUT LANES FIT IN ONE WITNESS by difference of squares: with lambda = r^2, 2a - 2b + 2*lambda*(c+d) - 1 - (r*(c+d) - (1-a+b))*(r*(c+d) + (1-a+b)) = xor2(a,b) + lambda*xor2(c,d) — ONE rank-1 row, verified for lambda = 4, 2 and 1. MEASURED per schedule step: 29 + 22 three-input lanes, 6 packed pairs and 1 singleton = 58 allocations and 57 rows covering all 64 lanes, against 64 + 64 for two separate XOR3 words. The singleton lane is then DEFERRED and shared across two adjacent steps by one more lambda = 2^40 packed row, so a PAIR of schedule steps is 182 allocations / 183 constraints. The 58 field elements recombine into the schedule sum affinely and the sigma words are never built as 32-bit vectors at all. DOES NOT APPLY to the ROUND sigmas Sigma0/Sigma1 — those are pure rotations with no degenerate lanes, so they stay at 32/32.

DECOMPOSE ONLY 7 OF 8 BITS PER MESSAGE BYTE, AND PAIR THE 8TH-BIT CHECKS. The top bit of a byte that is already an input signal is AFFINE in the byte and its low bits: hi := 128^-1*(byte - sum_{t<7} 2^t*low[t]). Witness only 7. THEN pack the remaining high-bit range checks TWO BYTES AT A TIME by difference of squares: centre each as x := (byte - lowSum) - 64*active so that x is in {-64, 0, +64} and x^2 = 4096*active, then settle two bytes in one row: (x0 - 1024*x1)*(x0 + 1024*x1) - 4096*(active0 - 1048576*active1) = 0, where the 1024^2 = 2^20 weight keeps the slots from interfering because |x| <= 64. MEASURED over 239 checked bytes: 1673 allocations (239 x 7) and 1793 constraints, i.e. 7 allocations + 7.5 constraints per byte against a naive 8 + 9 — saves 2.5 score per input byte.

THE #2 SUBMISSION (sleepdefic1t, 150537) IS AN ANCESTOR SNAPSHOT OF OUR 145479 SEED — ITS 109 FILES ARE A STRICT SUBSET OF OUR 145, AND OF 43 SHARED CostIs THEOREMS EXACTLY ONE DIFFERS. PackedMaj.main is 32 alloc / 64 constr for them against 32/32 for us; all 42 other gadgets are identical. Totals 72450+78087 = 150537 against 72449+73030 = 145479, delta 1 allocation + 5057 constraints. MECHANISM: they emit TWO forEach assertZero loops per packed-Maj lane, (z-(lambda+1)a)(z-(c+lambda*u)) = 0 and (z-(a+lambda*b))(z-(lambda*(a+b+u-1)+c)) = 0; we emit ONE using the out-of-range decoy root at Omega = 2^80, where the honest packed value is one root and the other is Omega-far and provably unabsorbable by the surrounding 35-bit addition. 32 constraints x (30 in block 1 + 32 per wide block x 4) = 5056. The residual 1+1 is the same trick at Round0Block1: they witness a carry bit plus a booleanity row plus a linear row; we emit residual*(residual + 2^32) = 0 with residual = fromBits(new_e) - fromBits(w) - eC. CONSEQUENCE: the decoy-root and half-a-row-per-bit entries are FULLY LANDED in our tree and are exactly what separates us from #2 — do not re-derive them and do not mine this rival further.

A FREE ASSUMPTION NOBODY HAS BANKED: messageLen < 256 IS ASSUMED, NOT ENFORCED. Challenge/Specs/SHA256.lean gives `Assumptions input len := IsByteArray input AND len < bufferLen` with bufferLen = 256 and len = input.messageLen.val. The byte-ness half is already exploited (it is what makes the 7-bits-per-byte decomposition complete), but the LENGTH BOUND IS NOT MENTIONED ANYWHERE IN THIS CORPUS — soundness only has to hold when it holds. AUDIT THE PADDING AND LENGTH PATH for any range check, bit decomposition or comparison on messageLen that exists ONLY to establish messageLen < 256; every such row is free score. NOTE WHAT THE ASSUMPTION DOES NOT GIVE: booleanity of the witnessed low bits is still needed (an adversary picks the bits), and the Spec's `if len <= bufferLen then output = sha256 (truncate input len) else False` still forces the digest words to be exact naturals, so the output decomposition stays.

HEADROOM VERDICT: RANK TWO OF SEVEN BY CONFIDENCE, ~12,500 AT STAKE, AND EXACTLY ONE UNRUN EXPERIMENT DECIDES IT. Record 145479 (ours). The per-round-pair budget is 658 = four upper sigmas 256 + four 32-bit decompositions 256 + packed Ch 64 + packed Maj 64 + fused adders 18. The decompositions are within 4 of the Bezout floor (63 per word marginal) and the adders are at 8 alloc / 10 constr for FOUR reductions, so essentially all remaining slack is the 256 spent on Sigma0/Sigma1. THE OPEN QUESTION IS ENTRY #1's AND IT HAS NEVER BEEN SWEPT: which PAIRS of single-row-native functions sharing inputs admit ONE lambda-packed row? Ch and Maj already reach 0.5 alloc + 0.5 constr per bit by pairing adjacent rounds; if any Sigma pairing does the same it is -128 per round pair = -4096 per block and roughly -17k overall, taking the circuit to ~128k. If the sweep comes back empty the circuit is essentially done at ~144k. THE SWEEP IS CHEAP (cvc5 QF_FF over the circom prime, same harness that classified 192 of 256 three-input functions as native) AND IT IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE-PER-COMPUTE ITEM ON THE WHOLE BOARD. Unconditional rank floor is 2 x 8 = 16; ignore it.

THE PACKING CRITERION, AND WHY SHA-256 SUPPLIES IT EXACTLY ONCE. A pair of gadget instances packs into ONE witness and ONE row essentially iff they SHARE AT LEAST TWO OF THEIR THREE INPUTS: xor3|xor3 and xor3|xor2 both pack at 2 shared inputs (the first via the two-root form, the second via a UNIQUE-ROOT non-vanishing-multiplier row, coefficients extracted and brute-force verified) and both fail at 0 or 1 shared inputs. Symmetry-reduced exhaustive sweep over all 256x256 pairs: at 0 shared inputs only 25 of 361 orbits pack, ALL via Case 1 and ALL with both functions of DIAGONAL-CORRECTED RANK 1 (a quadratic in a SINGLE affine form — the XOR2/AND2/OR2 family, 38 of the 256 three-input functions; this is exactly the difference-of-squares schedule packing we already run, and it is the ONLY disjoint packing that exists). At 1 shared input 297 of 1300 orbits pack but NOT ONE involves XOR3, Maj or Ch. At 2 shared inputs packing is abundant — which is where Ch and Maj live. NOW THE SHA-256 FACT, MEASURED EXHAUSTIVELY OVER EVERY LANE PAIR IN THE WHOLE CIRCUIT: no two materialised bit-gadget lanes reading the same word share more than ONE input bit. The offsets at which gadgets read a word are a-word {0 (Maj), 2,13,22 (Sigma0)}, e-word {0 (Ch), 6,11,25 (Sigma1)}, w-word {7,18,3-shift (sigma0), 17,19,10-shift (sigma1)}, and within every cohabiting gadget pair the PAIRWISE DIFFERENCES ARE ALL DISTINCT MOD 32, so one lane offset can align at most one input. Ch and Maj get their two shared inputs from a different mechanism entirely — the STATE ROTATION (a,b,c)->(new_a,a,b) and (e,f,g)->(new_e,e,f), an OFFSET-ZERO alignment. SHA-256 aligns two inputs in exactly one place and we already bank it. GENERAL RULE FOR OTHER HASHES: before attempting a packing, compute the multiset of pairwise differences of the offsets at which every gadget reads a shared word; a REPEAT is necessary for a pairing to exist.

HOW TO RUN A ROW-EXISTENCE QUERY — THE NAIVE ENCODING DOES NOT TERMINATE. Existentially quantifying all row coefficients and asserting the 2^n completeness equations TIMES OUT in cvc5 1.3.4 even at n=3, on plain XOR3. USE THE STAGED FORM: the degree->=3 part of the constraint is a LINEAR system over F_p in the unknown affine multiplier (B for the unique-root form, S for the two-root form) — solve it exactly by Gaussian elimination, and hand only the residual small bilinear degree-2 system to cvc5. That decides n=6 in MILLISECONDS. Non-vanishing of B is exact and cheap: over F_p a subspace is never covered by <= 2^n proper hyperplanes, so a non-vanishing B exists iff no cube point annihilates the whole solution space. VALIDATE ANY SUCH HARNESS against four known-good rows before trusting it: XOR3 native, AND3 non-native, PackedCh = Case 1, PackedMaj = Case 3; and re-verify every POSITIVE by extracting explicit coefficients and brute-forcing the cube. THE 192-OF-256 NATIVE CLASSIFICATION IS CONFIRMED with the exact criterion — f is native iff there is an affine M non-vanishing on the cube and an affine L with the multilinear reduction of M*(f+L) affine; the failure mode of all 64 non-natives is always that EVERY admissible M vanishes at some cube point; all 128 functions of GF(2) ANF degree <= 2 are native and exactly 64 of the 128 degree-3 ones are; the 'z = product of two affines + affine' subfamily is 70 functions and is a STRICT SUBSET of the 192.

CLOSED, NEGATIVE, PROVED — THE SIGMA CARRY WORD COSTS 64 AND THE SIGMAS ARE FINISHED. The word-level question was the last open lever: Sigma0(a) = rotr2+rotr13+rotr22 - 2*C (verified as an exact integer identity over 200000 random words), so everything reduced to 'what does ONE carry word cost'. IT COSTS 64 AND THAT IS NOW A THEOREM. C = sum_j 2^j*maj(a_{j+2},a_{j+13},a_{j+22}) is multilinear of degree EXACTLY 3 in the 32 input bits (128 monomials); an R1CS row is degree 2. (A) SINGLE PACKED WITNESS m = C: expanding (p*m+P0)(q*m+Q0) = r*m+R0 gives p*q*m^2 + B*m + (P0Q0-R0) = 0 with B affine. ML(C^2) has 400 DEGREE-6 MONOMIALS while ML(B*C) is degree <= 4 and P0Q0 is degree <= 2, so the two-root stage-1 solve is INFEASIBLE and p*q = 0 in every row; and the kernel of B -> [deg >= 3 part of ML(C*B)] over 33 columns and 3392 equations is EXACTLY {0}, so B = 0 in every row. Both coefficients vanish identically => NO ROW MENTIONS m => m is unconstrained => unsound, FOR ANY NUMBER OF ROWS. Identical for the xor materialisation and for Sigma1. (B) EVERY MULTI-LANE PACKING, ANY WEIGHTS, ANY ROW COUNT: two enumerated lemmas do the work — L1, the 928 4-sets {i} u T_j (i not in T_j) are pairwise distinct; L2, the 400 6-sets T_j u T_k (disjoint) are pairwise distinct; and there are ZERO four-lane subsets with a common bit or without a disjoint pair. So |J| >= 4 dies (L1 forces the multiplier constant, requiring degree <= 2; L2 leaves a degree-6 coefficient 8*c_j*c_k != 0). NOTE WHAT DID NOT BIND, EXACTLY AS PREDICTED: Theorem R gives only >= 2 and Theorem B is saturated by the input word's own 32 booleanity rows, so neither floor forbids < 64 — THE OBSTRUCTION IS THE DEGREE FILTRATION, and it is sharp. Three-lane packings split into exactly two orbits — STAR (J = {i-2,i-13,i-22}, the three lanes reading bit a_i, i.e. the 'three rotations share one source word' idea) and TRIANGLE (pairwise-sharing, no common bit) — both dead. THE STRENGTHENING THAT MATTERS: in every negative case BOTH stage-1 tests fail, so the result is not 'no SINGLE row' but 'NO ROW OF ANY KIND constrains the packed witness', which also kills the multi-row escape of covering the cube with several multipliers B_i that each vanish somewhere.

THE VERTEX-STAR TRICK: AN AND WORD OF TWO ROTATIONS COSTS 2*(MIN VERTEX COVER), NOT 2*32 — MEASURED, AND IT LOSES ON SHA-256's SIGMAS, SO BANK IT ELSEWHERE. Decomposing the Sigma carry word as C = val(A&B) + val(A&D) + val(B&D) - 2*val(A&B&D) exposes a clean structure: the lanes form 32 TRIANGLES on Z_32, and the edge graph is the 6-regular circulant C_32(9,11,20) for Sigma0 and C_32(5,14,19) for Sigma1, 96 edges each. Every AND lane is a product of two variables, so ALL edges incident to one vertex c pack into ONE row z_c = a_c * (sum of weighted neighbours) — a star, arbitrary weights, ONE allocation and ONE constraint — and the z_c recombine affinely. Covering all 96 edges therefore costs 2*(minimum vertex cover): measured independence number 9 for C_32(9,11,20) -> VC 23 -> 46 score, and 8 for C_32(5,14,19) -> VC 24 -> 48, for ALL THREE AND words at once, against 64 lane-by-lane. THE ROUTE STILL LOSES HERE because the cubic word val(A&B&D) survives: both endpoints of an edge determine its triangle uniquely, so a row a_c*z_c' yields at most ONE on-target cubic monomial plus garbage, i.e. >= 64 more, total >= 110 against the record's 64. GENERAL RULE WORTH CARRYING TO OTHER CHALLENGES: wherever a circuit needs a bitwise AND (or any degree-2 lane function) of two rotations or shifts of ONE word, build the STAR COVER of the difference-circulant instead of paying per lane — the saving is 2*(n - alpha). It fails on SHA-256 only because SHA-256 never needs an AND word on its own, only inside a degree-3 XOR3.

ALTERNATIVE STATE REPRESENTATIONS — ALL MEASURED, ALL WORSE (do not spend a slot re-deriving these). (a) PACKED BASE-8 DIGITS, the lookup-free analogue of the 'spread' trick: packing a lane as sum_i 8^i * A[i] is free, and summing 5 lanes gives digit values in [0,5] with no carries — but extracting each parity bit needs C and a quotient q in {0,1,2}, costing 128 allocations + 193 constraints per column-lane = score 321 against the current 256. Worse, because the 1-row XOR3 already handles its carry implicitly and there is no lookup-free way to range-check the digits more cheaply. (b) +/-1 FOURIER BASIS (b -> (-1)^b, XOR becomes multiplication): 3-input parity costs 2 rows instead of 1, 5-input 4 instead of 2 — uniformly about 2x worse, because the boolean encoding is exactly what lets L1/L2/M exploit booleanity. (c) AND-FIRST restructuring (materialise the 1600 chi ANDs and keep everything else GF(2)-linear): 6400 rows/round, because next-state bits become 33-term XORs.

CHI IS AT A PROVEN FLOOR, NOT JUST AN OBSERVED ONE: MC(chi5) = 5 is SAT-PROVED MINIMAL (Ko Stoffelen, 'Optimizing S-box Implementations for Several Criteria using SAT Solvers', FSE 2016, Table 1 — a proven minimum, not an upper bound; same table gives Ascon 5, ICEPOLE 6). Our chi costs 1600 rows/round = 5 rows per 5-bit S-box = exactly that floor, so NO better S-box decomposition exists. Caveat kept honest: a row is strictly more powerful than a GF(2) AND gate (XOR3 is 1 row and 0 ANDs), so MC is a heuristic floor for rows rather than a theorem — but here it is tight. By contrast MC(theta) = 0: every one of theta's 2240 rows/round is pure overhead from GF(2)-linearity not being F_p-linear.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER ARGUMENT OF MINE — 'R1CS ROWS ARE FACTORABLE QUADRICS SO ONE EQUATION CANNOT PIN TWO VARIABLES' IS TRUE PER ROW BUT FALSE ACROSS ROWS. The SPAN of two rows' quadratic parts need not split. Explicit counterexample, verified for p = 5,7,11,13,17,19,23,29,31,101,127: row 1 (z1+z2)(z1-z2) = z3 gives z1^2 - z2^2 = z3; row 2 ((d-1)*z2)*z2 = z3 gives (d-1)z2^2 = z3; together z1^2 = d*z2^2 with d a NON-RESIDUE forces z1 = z2 = z3 = 0 uniquely. So TWO rank-1 rows DO pin THREE unknowns. BN254 GOTCHA: p = 1 mod 4, so -1 IS a quadratic residue and x^2 + y^2 = 0 has nontrivial solutions — the least non-residue is 5, so use d in {5,7,10,11,14,15,17,19}. WHY IT STILL DOES NOT HELP, which is the useful part: Chevalley-Warning bounds the prize — r degree-2 rows in m unknowns with sum of degrees < m cannot have exactly one solution, so r >= ceil(m/2) and AT MOST A FACTOR 2 is ever available. And empirically it is not even that: over 1,140,029 sampled affine 3-cubes with uniquely-solvable fibers, two rows never pinned more than ONE affinely-independent function. Structurally, uniqueness with r < m forces the solution to be a singular point, the elimination gives a norm equation whose constant must vanish, and that forces the pinned values to be AFFINE in the inputs — i.e. values that were free anyway. CONCLUSION UNCHANGED, REASONING FIXED: stop looking for sub-one-row-per-non-affine-witness.

Contradiction, so the fused gate does not exist. GENERALISATION WORTH REMEMBERING: any single-row gadget whose function restricts on some subcube to a XOR of 4 or more free variables is impossible. Partial fusion (absorbing one D bit into chi's b0 slot only) survives the lemma but is useless, because every theta output bit is consumed in all three chi roles across the five S-boxes of its row and must be materialised anyway.

PROVED WITH SMT — THE SINGLE-ROW XOR STOPS AT 3 INPUTS (cvc5 QF_FF over the circom prime, harness validated against the known 3-input row before trusting the negative results). Question asked: does an n-input XOR admit ONE rank-1 row that pins z uniquely, i.e. L1 - (z + L2)*M = 0 with L1, L2, M affine in the boolean inputs and M non-vanishing on the cube? (This is the fully general single-row shape: a row quadratic in z has two roots and cannot pin z, so z must appear linearly, giving z*M = N with M affine non-vanishing.) COST DIAGNOSIS (derived — verify before trusting): the record 184320 = 1600 bits x 24 rounds x 4.8. The sibling GF(2) challenge does the SAME permutation shape at 2.0 per bit-round (1 allocation + 1 constraint = just chi's product). The whole 2.8/bit gap is XOR OVERHEAD: over the circom prime a XOR b = a + b - 2ab costs a MULTIPLICATION, whereas over GF(2) it is free addition. So the entire remaining win on this challenge is in how XOR is encoded — not in chi, whose multiplicative complexity is already minimal (5 per 5-bit row, SAT-proven).

SUM-THEN-EXTRACT-PARITY for wide XORs (the main lever): to XOR k bits over a large prime field, do NOT chain k-1 pairwise a+b-2ab products. Instead form S = b_1 + ... + b_k as a FREE affine combination (zero constraints), then extract S mod 2 by decomposing S into ceil(log2(k+1)) bits with one linear equation S = 2q + r; the parity bit r IS the XOR. Cost ~log2(k) allocations + booleanity instead of (k-1) multiplications. theta XORs 5 lane bits plus a rotated column parity (k~5-11), where log2 beats linear decisively — this is how theta becomes near-free in a NON-binary field.

FOLD BOOLEANITY INTO THE PRODUCT: if c = a*b with a,b already known boolean, c is automatically boolean — do NOT emit a separate c(c-1)=0 row. Likewise the parity bit from a sum-decomposition is forced boolean by the range argument. Every redundant booleanity row is a pure loss at 1 constraint each, and at 38400 chi outputs that is 38400 constraints if repeated.

DO-NOT-TRY, AND IT IS A TEMPTING ONE: XOR-GATE / SHORTEST-LINEAR-PROGRAM MINIMIZATION BUYS EXACTLY ZERO HERE. There is a large and still-active literature on minimizing the number of 2-input XOR gates needed to evaluate an F2-LINEAR MAP — the Shortest Linear Program problem: Boyar-Peralta, Tan-Peyrin (TCHES'20) adding randomization and 3-input XOR gates, the 'Superior Boyar-Peralta' (SBP) depth-aware heuristic, 'Improved Heuristics for Low-Latency Implementations of Linear Layers', and eprint 2025/1493 which revisits BP and cuts the AES linear layer from 91 to 89 g-XOR. Keccak's theta (and rho/pi, and SHA-256's Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1) are exactly such linear maps, so this looks like the obvious attack on the biggest remaining slack. IT IS NOT, BECAUSE AN XOR GATE COSTS NOTHING IN EITHER OF OUR COST MODELS. In native R1CS an affine combination lives inside the A/B/C vectors of a row and is free. In the GF(2) challenges the harness restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A and B AFFINE, so an arbitrary XOR-combination is free inside a multiplicand. Halving the XOR count of theta changes the score by ZERO. WHAT THETA'S 2240 ROWS PER ROUND ACTUALLY PAY FOR IS *MATERIALIZATION*, NOT XOR COUNT: a value costs an allocation exactly when it must appear as a BARE WITNESS VARIABLE — because it is a circuit output, or because its consumer needs a variable rather than an affine form. THEREFORE THE ONLY QUESTION WORTH ASKING IS: for each currently-materialized intermediate, WHO CONSUMES IT, and can that consumer take an affine form instead? Every row saved comes from deleting a materialization, never from restructuring the XOR tree that feeds it.

CONJUGATE-CIPHER CROSS-ROUND AMORTISATION: THE LINEAR CASE IS CLOSED, ONLY A NONLINEAR CONJUGATOR REMAINS OPEN. For the conjugated round C.F.C^-1 to still cost 1600 for chi, C must NORMALISE the chi layer (320 disjoint chi_5). The linear maps that do are generated by cyclic shifts within each 5-row and permutations of the rows — ALL PERMUTATION MATRICES — and conjugating the linear layer by a permutation is pure relabelling, leaving the row count identical. Any C not preserving the S-box structure turns chi into a generic 1600-output quadratic map and destroys the 1-row-per-bit gadget. Conjugating by L or by chi themselves merely rotates the round word cyclically and is cost-invariant. So the mechanism needs a genuinely NONLINEAR C whose own cost is paid twice over 1600 bits. Verified linear-algebra facts about L = rhoPi o theta, computed locally: rank(L) = 1600, rank(L - I) = 1598, rank(theta - I) = 319, L fixes the all-ones vector, dim ker(L^d - I) = 2d for d = 2,4,8,16 (a two-cycle permutation signature) — tempting but not exploitable for the reason above.

LAMBDA-PACKING AND THE TWO-ROOT DECOY DO NOT TRANSFER TO KECCAK, BECAUSE THIS CIRCUIT HAS NO BOUNDED-ARITHMETIC CONSUMER ANYWHERE. Both SHA-256 record tricks depend on the packed word being consumed ADDITIVELY by a modular adder, which splits the lambda slots for free and rejects the decoy at zero cost. In Keccak every consumer is a boolean gadget whose soundness needs each input as an IsBool value: from z = f_A + lambda*f_B neither half is an affine form, so a packed witness cannot feed a downstream Xor3Lane or ChiLane row (whose R1CS certificate requires AffineW inputs and whose soundness requires IsBool inputs). Any packing must be undone at cost, and a decoy root would simply satisfy the next row at a different value — UNSOUND rather than merely expensive. This does not formally close packing (a redesigned consumer reading the packed form directly is conceivable) but it is the precondition every packing proposal must answer first.

THE SINGLE-WITNESS ROW CRITERION — A CLOSED-FORM TEST THAT DECIDES, FOR ANY BOOLEAN FUNCTION AND ANY NUMBER OF ROWS, WHETHER ONE FRESH WITNESS SUFFICES. USE IT BEFORE PROPOSING ANY NEW GADGET ON ANY R1CS CHALLENGE — it is one linear-algebra solve and it is exact. DERIVATION (proved): a row is Q + A*B with Q,A,B affine in (inputs x, z). Put gamma(x) = R(x,0) and g(x) = R(x,1) - R(x,0) = q_z + a_z*b(x) + b_z*a(x) + a_z*b_z. Then (i) g is AFFINE IN x (+-1-Fourier degree <= 1) — the load-bearing constraint, which the earlier SMT formulation never exploited; (ii) completeness forces gamma = -f*g with deg gamma <= 2, hence deg(F*g) <= 2 where F = 1-2f; (iii) uniqueness at x needs some row's g(x) != 0, because R_i(x, 1-f(x)) = g_i(x)*F(x). THEREFORE z IS PINNABLE BY ANY NUMBER OF ROWS WITH ONE FRESH WITNESS IFF THE LINEAR SPACE G_f = {g affine : deg(F*g) <= 2} HAS NO COMMON ZERO ON THE CUBE. VALIDATED: exhaustive n=3 gives 192/256, reproducing the cvc5 QF_FF census in _common EXACTLY by an independent method, and both record gadgets land in the space (ChiLane's multiplier 4a+b+c-3 is exactly -g). RESULTS, exact rational arithmetic: XOR_n has dim G = 0 for ALL n >= 4 (general proof: F = u_1...u_n and deg g <= 1 give deg(F*g) >= n-1 > 2), so an n-input parity with n >= 4 CANNOT be pinned by one witness AT ANY ROW COUNT, not merely by one row. THE FULL THETA+CHI FUSION chi(b0,b1,b2) with each b_j a 3-XOR (9 inputs) has dim G = 0, because F's degree-9 Fourier term can only pair with |S| <= 1 and forces g = 0 — IMPOSSIBLE AT ANY ROW COUNT, strictly stronger than the restriction-lemma argument. PARTIAL FUSION IS ALSO IMPOSSIBLE, NOT MERELY USELESS: absorbing a single 2-XOR into chi's b0 slot gives dim G = 0; into b1 or b2 gives dim G != 0 but G has common zeros so z is not pinned; any 3-XOR into any slot, and the output-side form z = chi(a,b,c) XOR e, all give dim G = 0. NEW CENSUS AT n=4: 950/65536 functions certifiable, 264 essentially 4-ary — a genuine 4-input native gate library EXISTS — but every one has +-1-Fourier degree of F at most 3, while every keccak-relevant 4-input function (4-XOR, chi-plus-one-XOR) has degree >= 4. So no wider gate helps.

THE ONE CONCRETE SAVING THAT EXISTED HERE IS PROVED IMPOSSIBLE, AND Xor5Lane IS NOW PROVED OPTIMAL. THE LEVER, worth stating because it is the natural thing to try: score is allocations + constraints and a plain-R1CS row may have NO fresh witness, so a 5-input parity witnessing ONLY C and adding TWO assertion rows would cost 1 alloc + 2 constr = 3 per bit against Xor5Lane's 2 + 2 = 4 per bit — 320 C bits per round, -320/round, -7680 total, 184320 -> 176640 AND A LEADERBOARD. IT DOES NOT EXIST: by the single-witness row criterion XOR_n for n >= 4 has dim G = 0, so a 5-input parity cannot be pinned with one materialised witness at any row count. Two witnesses then force >= 2 rows by rank, so Xor5Lane's 128/128 (t = XOR3(a,b,c) then C = XOR3(t,d,e), Xor5Lane.lean.txt:21-23) IS THE EXACT OPTIMUM for an isolated 5-XOR. The 320 C bits of a round are parities of PAIRWISE-DISJOINT variable sets (column x, slice z), each needing ceil(4/2) = 2 three-input-XOR gates with no cross-column sharing possible, and each C is reused by exactly 2 D's — so ThetaC's 640/round is tight as a GF(2) 3-XOR addition chain (MODELLED for the no-cross-sharing step, a standard SLP direct-sum argument rather than a theorem).

MATERIALISATION CENSUS OF THE 184320 RECORD, AND THE PREMISE THAT KEEPS GETTING RE-PROPOSED AND IS FALSE. Per round the record materialises exactly four families and EVERY ONE IS READ: (a) 320 Xor5Lane intermediates t, read once each by the second Xor3Lane row of the same Xor5Lane (Xor5Lane.lean.txt:22-23); (b) 320 column parities C, read TEN times each by ThetaXor's Xor3Lane rows (ThetaXor.lean.txt:76 — lanes with x = x'+1 and x = x'-1, five lanes each); (c) 1600 theta outputs A', read THREE times each by ChiLane rows in the a/b/c roles (Chi.lean.txt:182-184, chiSource1/chiSource2 at BitwiseOps.lean.txt:61-66); (d) 1600 chi outputs, read by the next round's ThetaC and ThetaXor, or in round 23 exported through the free affine iotaWire. THERE IS NOT ONE VALUE MATERIALISED ONLY SO AN EQUATION CAN BE CHECKED AGAINST IT, so the secp 'assertion, not value' mechanism has NO SITE HERE: every materialised value is a boolean MULTIPLICAND SLOT of at least one downstream row, and that slot syntactically demands an affine form whose VALUE is a bit. NOW THE FALSE PREMISE, WHICH I PROPOSED MYSELF AND WHICH IS WORTH INOCULATING AGAINST: 'the theta output is A + C[x-1] + rot C[x+1], which is AFFINE in the state and the parities, so delete the 1600 theta materialisations.' IT IS GF(2)-AFFINE, NOT F_p-AFFINE, AND THE COST MODEL IS F_p. With bits encoded as field elements 0/1, A + Cl + Cr is a syntactically Affine EXPRESSION whose VALUE is the integer sum in {0,1,2,3}, not the XOR. The 1600 ThetaXor rows exist PRECISELY to convert the free affine sum into the non-affine XOR value; same for the 640 parities, a 5-XOR being a sum mod 2 of degree 5. WHENEVER A PROPOSAL SAYS 'XOR IS AFFINE SO IT IS FREE', CHECK WHICH FIELD IT IS AFFINE OVER — that confusion is the whole content of this challenge's 2.4x gap to the dimension floor. RESIDUAL OPEN GAP, STATED HONESTLY: the criterion covers systems with EXACTLY ONE fresh witness; a multi-witness multi-output gadget beating 2.4 materialisations per output bit is not excluded by anything above. But chi alone is at the SAT-proved MC(chi5) = 5 floor, theta's outputs are each read multiplicatively three times, and every single-witness fusion is dead — so there is no mechanism left to build one on. Allocate no slots.
