INCIDENTAL DATUM FOR THE THETA WORK: ThetaC's 640 rows are 2 per output bit for a 5-input XOR, and 2 is a floor for the single-row-native family — parameterising the row by the popcount s and demanding (parity(s) + a*s + b)(c*s + d) = e*s + f gives 6 equations in 5 projective unknowns at n = 5 (generically unsolvable) against 4 equations at n = 3, which is exactly why XOR3 is native and XOR5 is not. So any theta lever must come from NOT MATERIALISING C or NOT MATERIALISING the 1600 theta outputs, never from a cheaper XOR5 gadget.

EXTERNAL CALIBRATION: THE 184320 RECORD IS ABOUT TWICE AS GOOD AS PUBLISHED R1CS KECCAK, WHICH IS ANOTHER REASON NOT TO EXPECT A LITERATURE-DERIVED WIN HERE. Publicly documented R1CS Keccak-f1600 (Polyhedra, June 2025) reports theta 4480 constraints per round, rho and pi free, chi 3200, iota 64 — 7744 constraints per round and 185,856 CONSTRAINTS ALONE for the full permutation in Groth16. The record we are measured against is 92,160 allocations + 92,160 constraints = 184,320 TOTAL, i.e. 3840 constraints per round, so it is roughly 2x better on the constraint axis than the published figure and its SCORE is below what public practice spends on constraints alone. TWO SPECIFIC DIFFERENCES WORTH NAMING: the public account charges iota 64 constraints where iota is XOR WITH A COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT and therefore FREE AFFINE in this model; and it charges theta 4480 where the record's ThetaC + ThetaXor is 2240, because the record folds D away by making ThetaXor a 3-input XOR and never materialises it. THIS IS CALIBRATION, NOT A LEVER — it does not suggest anything to try. Its use is strategic: when a challenge's record already sits at half the published state of the art AND every gadget in it is at a proved floor, the prior that some paper contains an unexploited technique should be very low, and slots are better spent elsewhere.
rsa-pkcs1v15-sha256-4096-65537: HEAD-TO-HEAD MODMUL COUNTS ACROSS FOUR CODEBASES, ALL COMPILED AND MEASURED IN OUR MODEL (no lookups, no challenges), for one 256-bit a*b mod p over BN254: jsnark/xJsnark with a CONSTANT modulus and lazy range = 623 constraints at 32-bit chunks; jsnark with a variable modulus = 637 at 26-bit; arkworks r1cs-std emulated_fp = 680 (66 for mul_without_reduce + 614 for reduce) at 17 limbs x 15 bits; gnark v0.8.1 = 724 at 26x10 and 888 at its shipped 64x4. LIMB WIDTH 26-32 IS OPTIMAL AND 64 IS 18-22% WORSE — measured independently in two different codebases, and it reproduces xJsnark's own Figure 5 parameter sweep (b about 32 near-optimal, b = 120 about 40% worse). WE USE 4 LIMBS OF 64 BITS, i.e. the worst end of that curve; this is the same conclusion the pseudo-Mersenne analysis reached from a different direction, so treat 32-bit limbs as strongly corroborated. STRUCTURE OF THE COST, which is why: product limbs hinted and verified at 2n-1 FIXED points costs 2n-1 rows (15 at w=32) and is essentially free; q*p is FREE when p is a compile-time constant since constant scalings are linear; grouped carry propagation is 60-110; and ABOUT 80% OF THE WHOLE THING is bit-decomposition range checks on the quotient and remainder. LAZY REDUCTION IS WORTH ABOUT 600 CONSTRAINTS PER AVOIDED REDUCE (arkworks measures mul_without_reduce at 66 against reduce at 614, and additions cost literally zero), so a*b + c*d with one shared reduction is about 746 against 1360. FINALLY, WHY GNARK'S HEADLINE 99 CONSTRAINTS PER EMULATED MUL IS NOT AVAILABLE: modern gnark's mulMod emits ZERO constraints and defers to a Schwartz-Zippel check at a commitment-derived challenge (std/math/emulated/field_mul.go), and std/multicommit panics outright if the frontend is not a Committer — so it cannot even compile on a plain Groth16 frontend. Strip the challenge and the lookups and gnark's own pre-v0.10 code lands at 724.

PARAMETER TUNING — THREE OF THE FIVE CLOSURES NEEDED CORRECTING, AND ONE REVERSED. Karatsuba/Toom remains subsumed by evaluation at 2m-1 fixed points (Theta(m), below Karatsuba's m^1.58, interpolation free) — that one stands. The others: (a) SQUARING IS CHEAPER THAN MULTIPLICATION AFTER ALL, BUT NOT VIA tri(m). It is true that a(c)*a(c) costs the same one row per point as a(c)*b(c) IF every coefficient must be materialised. THE ESCAPE IS NOT TO MATERIALISE THEM: a grouped carry check only ever reads the 2K GROUP SUMS S_w = sum_{e<g} coeff(gw+e)*2^(Be), so it suffices to verify a GENERATING IDENTITY S(c) = beta(c)^2 + (c - t^9)*Hi(c) at 2K fixed points. For a SQUARE the high part Hi = sum_{i+j>=gw} h_i h_j is a SYMMETRIC staircase form of rank gw-1, so ceil((gw-1)/2) products suffice — 4 at gw = 9, realised in Lean as 2h8(A1-A4) + 2h7(A2-A4) + 2h6(A3-A4) + A5(2A4-A5) with A_k = sum_{j>=k} h_j. Cost 2m(1 + 1/gw) ~ 2m against 4m-3 for coefficient materialisation. MEASURED SAVING 294 per squaring, 4408 total — this IS the 326297 -> 321889 move. THE LIMIT OF THE TRICK IS EXACT: for a GENERAL product the staircase is BILINEAR of rank gw-1, needing gw-1 products, so the windowed cost is (2m/gw)*2*gw = 4m against 4m-3 — three units WORSE. It applies to the 15 chain squarings and provably cannot extend to q*n or to the final block's a^2*b. Tensor rank is the whole story: symmetry halves it, bilinearity does not. (b) MERGING SQUARINGS FAILS ON CARRY WIDTH, NOT ON WITNESS BITS. On bits alone merging is nearly neutral — a block covering k squarings needs 4096*(2^k - 1) quotient bits plus one 4096-bit residue = 4096*2^k for k squarings, so k=1 and k=2 TIE at 8192 per squaring and only k >= 3 is bit-worse. (My earlier '26302 against 18782' was wrong, and so is the record's own doc claiming exact cost-neutrality.) THE REAL OBSTRUCTION IS THE CARRY-WIDTH LAW w ~ (d-1)*B + log2(g*d*m), where d is the DEGREE of the verified product — VERIFIED AGAINST MEASUREMENT: d=2, B=24, g=9, m=171 gives model 35.6 against measured max 33 (the balanced representation buys ~2.6); d=3, B=16, g=13, m=256 gives model 45.3 against measured max 47. Merging two squarings takes d from 2 to 4, so w jumps by a whole B, the group budget w + B*g <= 253 collapses from g=9 to g=7, and the carry cost per squaring goes 2267 -> 8121 at B=24 (4243 even at B=12). COROLLARY THAT EXPLAINS A DESIGN CHOICE: the final block runs at B=16 rather than the chain's B=24 precisely because it verifies a DEGREE-3 product, where halving B removes about B bits of carry width. (c) THE LIMB WIDTH IS A FLAT OPTIMUM — RETIRE THE 'b=17 BEATS b=24 BY 0.9%' CLAIM. Contradicted three ways. The record's own measured pre-window sweep has B=24 as a SHARP local minimum (20:20120, 22:20124, 23:20260, 24:20006, 25:20283, 26:20248, 28:20140). A post-window model calibrated on the measured B=24 point (3361 modelled against 3328 measured, 1% high) is flat across 16..24: 16:3363, 17:3351, 18:3359, 20:3318, 22:3374, 24:3361, 26:3588, 32:4052 — best case about 43 per squaring, ~645 total, inside the model error. And B MUST BE A MULTIPLE OF 8 or the free byte-to-limb packing breaks. Fully built-out but ABANDONED Params32.lean (B=32, 129 limbs) and Params24Final.lean show the sweep was done empirically. DO NOT RE-OPEN THE LIMB WIDTH.

WHERE THE COST ACTUALLY IS, AND WHY IT IS HARD TO MOVE: about 82% of each modmul is TWO 4096-bit range checks — the quotient q and the remainder r, roughly 8037 rows each at b=24 — with grouped carries about 2627 and the evaluation rows about 1364. THE OBVIOUS ATTACK FAILS FOR TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS. Dropping the quotient range check (letting the carry bounds force q small) is INCOMPATIBLE WITH GROUPED CARRIES: grouping bounds only the group sums, not the individual coefficients, so you would need one carry per coefficient — 12276 bits per op instead of 1368, a net loss of about 21800 against the 8037 saved. It is also UNSOUND for adversarial n: if every limb of n is even, take q0 = 1/2 mod p and every (q*n)_i is a 23-bit value, the carry chain passes, and the circuit accepts a*b - r = n/2. RNS/CRT is likewise dead in plain R1CS — reducing modulo an auxiliary prime needs a witnessed quotient of full bit length, costing at least what it saves; RNS only pays when range checks are lookups. Barrett vs Montgomery is irrelevant because the quotient is nondeterministic advice, so there is no division to optimise. AND THE RANGE CHECK ITSELF IS OPTIMAL: a k-bit check costs 2k-1 (k rows + k-1 allocations) and that is a lower bound — r rank-1 rows cut a variety whose projection has degree at most 2^r by Bezout, so at most 2^r values can be accepted. The top-bit-fold already attains it; base-4 or base-8 digit decompositions tie at best.

RETRACTION — THE BYTE-WISE RANGE-CHECK LEVER DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE ARRAYS IT TARGETED ALREADY COST ZERO. Two independent errors in my earlier note. (1) THE MODULUS AND SIGNATURE RANGE CHECKS ARE ALREADY FREE: `costIs_sub_bytes24ToBigInt` is `Count.zero`, because the limbs are affine in the input bytes and the byte bounds come from the challenge Assumptions (IsOctetString). There is nothing there to save. PadDigest24 is likewise Count.zero, and the REASON is worth knowing: B = 24 is BYTE-ALIGNED (3 bytes per limb), so packing is affine — the legacy PadDigest at limbBits = 121 has to witness 14 split bits plus 16 booleanity rows, while PadDigest24 witnesses nothing. (2) The 512 x (2*8 - 1) = 7680 arithmetic is wrong for a FRESH witness. The 2k-1 form (k-1 allocations + k rows via the top-bit fold) is available only when there is an already-allocated or affine expression to fold the top bit against. For a fresh k-bit witness Bezout gives BOTH bounds — r quadrics in A^a have at most 2^a isolated solutions so a >= k, and the projection has degree at most 2^r so r >= k — hence 2k exactly, and splitting into 512 independently-checked chunks cannot beat it because each chunk then needs its own allocation. MEASURED: the record's quotient check is 4095 allocations + 4095 rows = 8190 = 2*4095, and its remainder check is 8192 = 2*4096. Both are AT the floor, not at 8037. Total slack across all 31 range checks in the circuit: 31 units.

CORRECTION — THERE IS NO SHA-256 IN THIS CIRCUIT. Verified against the challenge interface: `digest : Vector F digestBytesLen` is an INPUT ('SHA-256 digest of the message being verified'), and the seed solution contains zero hash/compression files — every module is bigint machinery (SqMulModBal, ModExpSq, GroupedEq*, EqViaCarries, MixedRadix, Bytes*). The published '66% SHA-2 / 14% bigint' split for RS256 circuits does NOT apply here because those circuits hash the message and this one does not. ALL ~326k of the cost is non-native bigint arithmetic: the 16 squarings + 1 multiply mod a 4096-bit N, plus byte<->limb conversion and the padding comparison. Optimise the modmul and the limb/carry machinery; do not go looking for a hash to shrink.
Exponent 65537 = 2^16 + 1: exactly 16 squarings + 1 multiply; every step is a fixed-modulus modmul — share reduction machinery across all 17.
Fixed modulus: precompute q'[0] (Montgomery -N^{-1} mod 2^w), R^2 mod N, and all modulus limbs as circuit CONSTANTS — no in-circuit inverse or per-op setup.
CIOS/Montgomery with carry elimination: when the top modulus word is bounded ((D-1)/2-1), the t[N]/t[N+1] carries are provably zero, dropping ~5N+2 additions per multiply (gnark result).
Limb count sweet spot N<=12 wide limbs; minimize the number of carries that need range checks — each naive range check costs ~1/2 constraint per bit, so wider limbs with fewer carries win.
CRT / RNS residue representation to split the 4096-bit reduce into independent smaller-modulus channels; recombine once at the end.
Only range-check the modular residual, the quotient coefficient, and carries — not every intermediate; use top-bit-fold range checks.

LAZY REDUCTION with static limb-bound tracking (xJsnark long-integer arithmetic): carry a compile-time upper bound per limb and let partial products accumulate in wider limbs; emit a carry-normalization + range check ONLY when a limb's tracked bound would exceed field capacity, instead of normalizing after every op. Across the 16 squarings + 1 multiply this removes whole normalization passes, not just individual carries.

DEFERRAL BUDGET, concretely (circom-ecdsa): with n-bit limbs and k of them, unreduced accumulation is safe while 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < (native field bits). Use this inequality to place carry/reduce passes at the LAST legal moment instead of guessing; multiples of the fixed modulus used to reduce are compile-time constants.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce): keep products unreduced in wide limbs and reduce once per accumulated expression, not per multiply. CAUTION: bellman-bignat [OWWB20] and similar bigint libraries are tuned for constraint DENSITY, not constraint COUNT — do not copy their limb layout without re-costing it against allocations+constraints.

mulmod as ONE polynomial-identity check at a single constant point (gnark/eprint 2025/933): hint quotient q and error/carry limbs e out of circuit, then enforce a(X)b(X) = c(X) + alpha(X)q(X) + (2^B - X)e(X) evaluated at ONE fixed X=2^B — collapses the full limb-by-limb equality into a single rank-1 product plus range checks on q,c,e, instead of one constraint per limb coefficient. Evaluate-at-a-point beats coefficient-matching in this R1CS metric; reuse the same hinted-then-checked shape for all 17 squarings/multiplies.

PKCS1v15 padding is almost entirely CONSTANT: the 0x00 01 FF...FF 00 prefix and the DigestInfo DER header are fixed bytes. Comparing the recovered padded block against them costs only affine equality checks against constants — allocate nothing for the padding bytes themselves, and never range-check a byte whose value is fixed by the spec.

CORRECTION + PROOF — THE RANGE CHECK IS EXACTLY AT ITS FLOOR, AND THE FLOOR ARGUMENT IN OUR CORPUS WAS ONLY HALF AN ARGUMENT. MEASURED FROM Solution/.../CostBal.lean squareModBalGTCount at m=171,B=24,tq=15,tw=16,G=39: one middle/first squaring is 9836 alloc + 9874 constr = 19710, split as q-certification 8190, r-certification 8192, grouped carries 2267, window 380, evaluation 681. THE TWO CERTIFICATION FIGURES ARE EXACTLY 2x THE BIT-LENGTH: q is 170*24+15 = 4095 bits and costs 8190; r is 170*24+16 = 4096 bits and costs 8192. Zero slack, not 'roughly 8037'. (Also correct in that entry: grouped carries are 2267 not 2627, and the evaluation block is 681 = (2m-2) alloc + (2m-1) constr, not 1364.) THE CORPUS JUSTIFICATION ('r rank-1 rows cut a variety whose projection has degree at most 2^r by Bezout') BOUNDS ROWS ONLY AND THEREFORE PROVES ONLY HALF OF 2k-1. THE MISSING HALF IS A DIMENSION ARGUMENT: by Heintz's Bezout inequality, r quadrics in A^N have sum-of-component-degrees at most 2^min(r,N), so a gadget whose accepted set for a designated affine form is finite of size 2^k needs BOTH r >= k rows AND N >= k coordinates. With the value itself already allocated the marginal cost is (k-1) allocations + k rows = 2k-1, and that is exactly what RangeCheck.mainBits emits. SUPERSETS DO NOT HELP AND SLACK STRICTLY COSTS: an accepted set of size 2^(k+s) costs >= 2(k+s), and completeness forces size >= 2^k, so 2k is the floor for any finite acceptor regardless of how loose it is. BASE-4/BASE-8 DIGITS TIE EXACTLY (not 'at best'): the degree-2^k root set built by composing quadratics, w1 = z^2+az, w2 = w1^2+..., final w_{k-1}(w_{k-1}-c) = 0, is k-1 allocations + k rows = 2k-1, identical to booleanity. THE F_p-SPECIFIC ESCAPE HATCH (the 'true per row, false across rows' failure mode) WAS CHECKED AND CLOSES: restricting a field element to a multiplicative coset of index d via y^d = z costs about 2*log2(d) — again exactly 2 per bit — and yields a coset, not an interval, so it cannot certify integer smallness. HONEST SCOPE: this is a bound on a GADGET that pins a value to a finite set. It is NOT a lower bound on the modmul or on the circuit; see the global-floor entry.

THE QUOTIENT RANGE CHECK IS NECESSARY FOR EVERY MODULUS, NOT ONLY FOR EVEN-LIMB ONES — CORRECTING OUR OWN ATTACK WRITE-UP. Our corpus says dropping it 'is also UNSOUND for adversarial n: if every limb of n is even, take q0 = 1/2 mod p'. That understates it by a lot. VERIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION at toy scale (p = 2^61-1, B=4, m=8 limbs, carry groups of 4): with the quotient limbs left as unconstrained field elements, the map q -> (grouped carry sums of (q*n)) is F_p-LINEAR from F_p^m to F_p^(m/gw), i.e. 8 unknowns against 4 equations, so it is surjective for essentially every n and the adversary simply SOLVES for q. 200 out of 200 random trials with ODD, top-bit-set n produced a full forgery: an arbitrary chosen r != a^2 mod n accepted, with all carries set to zero. At our real parameters it is 171 free field unknowns against 37 group equations — even more underdetermined. So the even-limb story is a cute special case, not the reason; the real reason is a dimension count, and it means NO relaxation of the quotient certification survives as long as the carry chain is grouped. Corollary: an F_p convolution coefficient (q*n)_j only has an integer meaning if q_j is certified below 2^B, and that is the whole of why the check exists.

THE RANGE-BIT CONSERVATION LAW — THE SINGLE MOST DECISION-RELEVANT FACT ABOUT THIS CHALLENGE, AND IT KILLS BATCHING, LAZY REDUCTION AND MERGED SQUARINGS IN ONE LINE. For any reduction node certified by a witnessed integer identity P = q*n + r, the certification cost is 2*(bits(q) + bits(r)) = 2*bits(P), because bits(q) = bits(P) - bits(n) and bits(r) = bits(n). SO THE COST OF A REDUCTION IS EXACTLY TWICE THE BIT-LENGTH OF THE PRODUCT IT REDUCES, and nothing about how the reduction is organised changes it. CONSEQUENCES, all checked numerically. (1) A node fusing M reduced 4096-bit residues under one quotient costs exactly 8192*M, so the whole exponentiation's certification cost is 8192*(sum of arities), independent of the shape of the DAG. (2) MERGING TWO SQUARINGS IS EXACTLY COST-NEUTRAL on certification, not a loss — x^4 = q*n + r has bits(q)+bits(r) = 12288+4096 = 16384, identical to two separate squarings at 8192 each. Our corpus entry blames 'the quotient grows to 12288 bits'; that is the wrong reason. The real reason merging loses is the EVALUATION block, which grows like (M-1)^2 (measured: 4m-3 cells at M=2, 16m-9 at M=3). Merging three or more IS a certification loss: 4096*2^k against 8192*k. (3) LAZY / DEFERRED REDUCTION IS WORTH ZERO HERE, and this is why the secp figures do not transfer. Sharing one reduction across M products pays off only for a SUM of products (sum_i a_i b_i has a quotient of just 4096 + log2 M bits), and affine EC formulas are sums of products. A modular exponentiation chain contains no additions at all — every step is a single product — so there is nothing to share. Do not port the '424 rows at M=1, 457 at M=2' curve from the secp entries to this challenge. (4) MEASURED TOTAL: 15 squarings at 16382 certification each plus the fused final node at 16382 = 262112, which is 80.3% of our 326297 and 81.4% of the 321889 record. Everything else in the circuit — all carries, all evaluation rows, all byte packing — is the remaining 19%.

THE MULTI-ARITY REDUCTION DAG IS THE RIGHT COST METRIC, NOT 'NUMBER OF MODMULS', AND OUR CURRENT SHAPE IS PROVABLY OPTIMAL UNDER IT. Our corpus says '17 MULTIPLICATIONS IS PROVABLY OPTIMAL' from l(65537) >= 17. That is true and irrelevant: our own record does 16 reduction nodes, not 17, because the last square and the last multiply are FUSED into one arity-3 certificate a*a*b = q*n + em (SqMulModBalTo, measured 12955+13018 = 25973 at m=256,B=16, with the residue FREE because em is an affine form of the digest). The correct objective is sum-of-arities. FORMALLY: a reduction node of arity M sums M previously-computed exponents at cost C(M), so the reachable exponent after nodes M_1..M_k is at most prod M_i, and 65537 needs prod M_i >= 65537. Calibrated cost model (fitted exactly to the two real gadgets in the tree: C(2) = 8192*2 + 4m + carry = 19147 at the best limb width, C(3) = 34511, C(3) with free residue = 26319 against the measured 25973): rate C(M)/ln M is 27625 at M=2, 31414 at M=3, 39839 at M=4 — arity 2 has the best rate, so arity 3 only pays where it saves a whole node. EXHAUSTIVE RESULT: of all arity multisets with product >= 65537, EXACTLY ONE is cheaper than our current shape — thirteen arity-2 nodes plus two arity-3 nodes, 309741 against 313524, a 1.2% gap — and a complete DFS over every chain of at most 15 nodes with arities in {2,3} proves NO such chain reaches 65537 exactly. (Product 2^13*9 = 73728 clears the bound but the exponent is not attainable.) Everything involving an arity-4 or arity-5 node is strictly worse. CONCLUSION: 15 squarings + one fused arity-3 tail is optimal, and there is ZERO headroom in the exponentiation structure. Stop looking at addition chains, windowing and merged squarings; they are all closed.

THE MODULUS IS AN INPUT — READ FROM Challenge/Instances/.../Interface.lean, NOT INFERRED. `structure Input (F) where modulus : Vector F 512; digest : Vector F 32; signature : Vector F 512`. All three are public inputs; the modulus is fully adversarial. THE ONLY THINGS Assumptions GIVES US (Specs/RSASSAPKCS1v15.lean): IsOctetString on modulus, digest and signature, and HasBitSize (os2ip n) 4096, i.e. 2^4095 <= N < 2^4096. THERE IS NO ODDNESS, NO PRIMALITY, NO gcd CONDITION, NO CO-PRIMALITY WITH e. An all-even-byte modulus such as N = 2^4095 satisfies Assumptions exactly. SO THE FOLLOWING ARE ALL DEAD: precomputed multiples of N as compile-time constants, constant-folded reductions, modulus-shape-specific folds, pseudo-Mersenne tricks, Orup-style modulus rescaling to N~ = -1 mod 2^k, casting-out-primes with a free native leg. WHAT SURVIVES AND IS ALREADY USED: N's limbs are inputs, so ANY affine function of them (3N, N shifted, a balanced-representative offset proportional to N) is a free linear combination and costs nothing — the balanced-residue window already exploits 2^4095 <= N to buy one bit off the middle quotient (tq = 15, not 16). SECOND CONSEQUENCE, WORTH MORE THAN IT LOOKS: because IsOctetString is ASSUMED and not checked, the modulus, signature and digest bytes need NO range check at all — Bytes24ToBigInt.circuit and PadDigest24.circuit are both literally Count.zero. Our corpus entry proposing to 'range-check the BYTES rather than the limbs of the modulus and signature, saving about 357 each' is chasing a check that does not exist; the 8037/8190 figures are the QUOTIENT and RESIDUE certifications inside each squaring, not input checks. Nothing to save there.

WEB PASS, FOUR TOPICS, ALMOST ENTIRELY DRY — RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-SEARCHES. (1) BATCHED / AMORTIZED RANGE PROOFS WITHOUT LOOKUPS OR CHALLENGES: none exist. Bulletproofs/BP+/BP++ aggregation shrinks PROOF SIZE only, never the multiplication-gate count, and needs Pedersen commitments plus challenges. Sharp (CCS'22), CKLR21 bounded integer commitments, Daza-Rafols-Zacharakis updateable IPA, lattice amortized shortness — all need challenges, vector commitments or hidden-order groups. ZNARKs (SNARKs over the integers) do give the dream 4-constraint range check but need an integer commitment, a random prime challenge AND an unknown-order group. (2) SUM-OF-SQUARES RANGE PROOFS (Boudot, Lipmaa, Groth 4x+1 = a^2+b^2+c^2, Couteau-Peters-Pointcheval) ARE CHALLENGE-FREE AND ALGEBRAIC — and VACUOUS over F_p, because every element of a finite field is a sum of TWO squares, so the R1CS is satisfiable for every x. The only repair is to range-check each w_i, which costs 1.5x to 3x more than checking x directly. This is the most tempting-looking dead end in the space; it is definitively dead. (3) PROOF-OF-EXPONENTIATION (Wesolowski, Pietrzak, BBF PoE/PoKE, Block et al., Gerbicz-Li, all batch PoEs) DIES TWICE: every one needs a verifier-chosen prime or challenge, AND every one has verifier cost Omega(lambda) group operations, i.e. 128+ modmuls against our 17. Wesolowski literally DEGENERATES at e = 65537: for any lambda >= 17 the challenge prime exceeds the exponent, so q = 0, pi = 1, and the verifier's check IS the original exponentiation. Schul-Ganz and Segev (TCC 2020) prove a matching generic-group LOWER BOUND that non-trivial non-interactive batch verification is impossible, which is as close to an impossibility theorem for this direction as exists. Delegation/outsourcing of modular exponentiation (Hohenberger-Lysyanskaya, Chen et al.) is probabilistic (1/2, 2/3 checkability) AND needs client-held secret randomness — structurally impossible inside a circuit. (4) HARDWARE MODMUL LITERATURE, READ ALGEBRAICALLY: Orup quotient pipelining looks like a huge win ('the quotient digit is literally the low limb of the accumulator') and IS NOT — determining the quotient was never our cost, the quotient is free advice; CERTIFYING it is the cost, and Orup does not change bits(q)+bits(r). Adopting it would force us to materialise n intermediate accumulators, i.e. n^2 limb certifications. Walter's no-final-subtraction invariant and o1js 'almost reduced' top-limb bounds are both already the balanced-residue design we run. Negre-Plantard-Robert's n(n+1)/2 squaring saves LIMB PRODUCTS, which are free for us at 2m-1 evaluation points. Bipartite/tripartite modular multiplication is parallelism-only. CONFIRMED: no published R1CS constraint count for RSA-4096 exists anywhere (checked zk-email, circom-rsa-verify, halo2-rsa, noir_rsa, noir-bignum, zkPassport, gnark, xJsnark, Cinderella). Best real comparables: Ozdemir et al. USENIX'20 7563 constraints per 2048-bit modmul with a CONSTANT modulus; xJsnark 88949 for the whole RSA-2048 e=65537 modexp with a hardcoded modulus; circom-rsa-verify 536212 for RSA-2048 including SHA-256. Our 321889 for RSA-4096 with a VARIABLE modulus almost certainly remains the best number in existence.

THE HONEST GAP, STATED PRECISELY, BECAUSE IT IS THE ONLY PLACE A BIG WIN CAN STILL LIVE. Everything above proves that our GADGETS are at their floors and that the CHAIN SHAPE is optimal. None of it is a lower bound on the CIRCUIT. The accepted set of public inputs is {(n, h, s) : 2^4095 <= N < 2^4096, s < n, s^65537 = EM(h) mod n}, of size about 2^(4095+256) = 2^4351, since for almost every (n,h) there is at most one s. Applying the same Heintz/Bezout counting to the whole circuit gives rows >= 4351 and (public inputs + witnesses) >= 4351, so with 1056 public field elements the floor is about 3295 + 4351 = 7646 in score. WE PAY 321889 — FORTY-TWO TIMES THE FLOOR. Nothing information-theoretic forbids a vastly cheaper circuit. What forbids it, concretely, is one thing and only one thing: the F_p convolution coefficient (q*n)_j has an integer meaning only if q_j is certified below 2^B, and the only known certifications of integer smallness in a prime field cost 2 per bit. Every technique that beats that rate — lookups, log-derivative/logup, Schwartz-Zippel at a challenge point, casting out primes with a free native leg, integer commitments, hidden-order groups — is excluded by this challenge's model, and we verified externally that the literature contains nothing else. The Bezout floor for the joint object is only about 2*8192 = 16384, since the entire witness is determined by (s, n), so nothing in our lower-bound machinery rules it out. Neither a construction nor an impossibility proof was found, in our work or in the literature. That is the one live question; everything else in this file is closed.

THE 4-DIM CONSTRUCTION IS THE RIGHT ONE and the extra two lattice dimensions come from NON-DETERMINISTIC ADVICE, not from the curve: hint Q = [s]P and verify a relation, which makes the kernel lattice rank 4 with determinant n and all four coefficients about n^(1/4). GENERAL LAW, matching gnark-crypto's own documented bounds to within half a bit: allowing t points in the verified relation gives rank 2t, determinant n^(t-1), coefficients Theta(n^((t-1)/(2t))) — 1.15*sqrt(r) at t=1, 1.25*r^(1/4) at t=2, 1.28*r^(1/3) at t=3. Per-iteration cost is nearly FLAT in dimension (3727/3810/4104 rows per iteration at 2/4/6 dims), so in-circuit cost is essentially iterations x constant and iterations = bit length. This is why the software result of eprint 2025/1151 (three scalars of a third the size, ~20% faster verification) DOES NOT TRANSFER to circuits, and why gnark ships the 6-dim variant only for NATIVE twisted Edwards with LogUp, never for emulated curves. MEASURED TARGET FOR THE MODMUL: 845 SCORE, AGAINST OUR 1463 (mulModSub2Cost = 728 alloc + 735 constr). These numbers come from actually compiling circuits with circom 2.2.3 and reading row counts out of the .r1cs with snarkjs, then witness-testing on 508 vectors including the worst case (p-1)^2 — not from a paper. Reference points, as rows + allocations: circom-ecdsa BigMultModP(64,4) = 7707; circom-pairing FpMultiply(43,6) at secp256k1 = 2509; fold with tightened carry parameters at n=32,k=8 = 1527; FOLD + CRT at n=32,k=8 = 845 (424 rows + 421 allocs). THREE INGREDIENTS, IN ORDER OF IMPORTANCE. (1) THE PRODUCT IS ALREADY FREE — the full 256x256 limb product is 2k-1 rows by asserting the limb-polynomial identity at 2k-1 evaluation points (circom-ecdsa's BigMultNoCarry is 7 rows), so 99.8% of a naive BigMultModP is carries and range checks and NO effort should go into the multiplication. (2) THE FOLD IS FREE FOR EVERY MODULUS — reducing the 2k-1 product limbs back to k via precomputed constants 2^(n(k+i)) mod p is a LINEAR COMBINATION, zero rows. What p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977 buys is that the fold coefficients are TINY (literally 977 and 1 when n = 32, because c = 2^32 + 977 is limb-aligned there), which cascades: folded limb width 77 bits instead of 101, quotient bound 36 bits instead of 68, CRT limbs 2 instead of 3, carry width 46 instead of 70 — worth about 27% (424 vs 578 rows for a generic 256-bit prime, both compiled). USE n = 32 PRECISELY BECAUSE c IS LIMB-ALIGNED THERE. (3) THE BIG ONE — CHECK THE IDENTITY BY CRT, NOT BY A CARRY CHAIN (Lubarov and Baylina, 'Casting out Primes', eprint 2022/1470): verify under a FIXED set of moduli M = {r_BN254, 2^(nT)} and conclude the identity holds mod lcm(M), which suffices when |f| < lcm(M). NOTE THIS NEEDS NO RANDOM CHALLENGE — the moduli are fixed constants, so it maps to plain R1CS. Mod r_BN254 the check R - p*X - out = 0 is ONE PURELY LINEAR ROW because the modulus is a CONSTANT; mod 2^(nT) only T = 2 carries at 46 bits are needed instead of a full chain of 8. Soundness margin measured at 25 bits (|D|max = 2^293 < r*2^64 = 2^318) and brute-forced on scaled-down analogues. CAVEAT FOR RSA: there the modulus is an INPUT, so p*X is a genuine product and the native leg is NOT free — this transfers to the secp challenges much better than to RSA.

SPARSE-PRIME CANONICITY IS 8 ALLOCATIONS + 11 CONSTRAINTS GIVEN THE BITS — MY EARLIER '37 ROWS' WAS 2x TOO HIGH. Comparing an already-decomposed 256-bit value against p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977 needs neither a subtraction nor a generic lexicographic comparator, because p's binary expansion has ONLY SIX ZERO BITS (positions 32, 9, 8, 7, 6, 4) and everything else is 1. So x < p iff some all-one run of p contains a zero of x, checked as a short prefix chain: (1) topEq <- IsZeroField(sum of deficit bits over positions 255..33), then one row topEq*b[32] = 0; (2) midEq <- IsZeroField(deficit over 31..10), throughMid <== topEq*midEq; (3) ONE row throughMid*(b[9]+b[8]+b[7]+b[6]) = 0 — four boolean bits sum below the native modulus, so one row enforces all four; (4) through5 <== throughMid*b[5]; (5) lowEq <- IsZeroField(deficit over 3..0), one row through5*(b[4] + lowEq) = 0. TOTAL 8 allocations / 11 constraints ON TOP of the decomposition = 19 score, against 260/265 for Normalize + LessThan. THE METHOD IS GENERIC: count the ZERO bits of the modulus, summarise each all-one run with one IsZeroField, chain the prefix-equality state with one product per run boundary — rows scale with the number of ZERO BITS of p, not with 256.

THE PSEUDO-MERSENNE QUOTIENT FOLD IS NOW IMPLEMENTED AND IT WAS THE WHOLE 36% CUT — MY EARLIER ESTIMATE UNDERSTATED IT. p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977, so 2^256 = cFold = 2^32 + 977, and the 7 product cells fold onto 4 by d_k = c_k + cFold*c_{k+4} — a FREE linear recombination because cFold is a compile-time constant. THE POINT IS WHAT THAT DOES TO THE QUOTIENT: instead of witnessing q as a 4-limb BigInt and paying a 252-row Normalize on it, q becomes ONE FIELD ELEMENT WITH A 71-BIT RANGE CHECK, and the carry chain collapses from 3 carries at 68 bits to ONE carry at 107 bits (grouped schedule L=6, groups [2,1,3], G=3). Across 350 live certificates that is 196,700, which is essentially the entire 559597 -> 355748 improvement. I also predicted GroupedEqXV would be 'a wash'; it is better than a wash. PER-STEP MULTIPLICATION COUNT IS AT THE FLOOR AND THE RECORD CONFIRMS IT — only the absolute numbers moved. Affine add is 3 certificates, generic double 4, triple 6, and the fused 2P+Q is 5 because it omits y of the intermediate. The record's FusedStep is now 2346 allocations / 2371 constraints (it was 3782 before the quotient fold) and is still EXACTLY 5 certificates: 3 multiply-subtracts at 448/453 and 2 fused divisions at 476/481. Those 5 certificates are 4617 of the step's 4717 score — 97.9%. CONSEQUENCE: per-step structural cleverness is spent; everything now rides on the cost of a single certificate, which is 95.8% range-check bits (508 for the result's canonicality, 141 for the 71-bit quotient, 214 for the 107-bit grouped carry).

CALIBRATION — OUR NUMBERS APPEAR TO BE THE ONLY PLAIN-R1CS ONES IN EXISTENCE. circom-ecdsa ECDSAVerifyNoPubkeyCheck(64,4) is 1508136 constraints and its fixed-base ECDSAPrivToPub is 95444 (stride 8, 32 windows, 256-entry tables); subtracting gives roughly 1.39-1.40M for its variable-base scalar multiplication. Against that our 559597 and 80147 are about 2.5x and 1.2x better. Everything smaller in the literature is out of scope: gnark's 100914 for [s]P uses logUp range checks plus a multicommit challenge; spartan-ecdsa's 3039 proves over secq256k1 where the field is NATIVE; halo2-ecc is PLONKish and lookup-driven. The one transferable idea from spartan-ecdsa is the efficient-ECDSA transform (two scalar multiplications down to one), which is R1CS-neutral and orthogonal to this challenge.

THE Y-FREE (x, lambda) LOOP IS 4 CERTIFICATES NOT 5 AND IS WORTH ~55k — BUT IT IS BLOCKED BY THE IDENTITY TABLE ENTRY, SO DO NOT ATTEMPT IT BEFORE RECODING. This replaces my earlier note that simply called it the biggest lever; the algebra is better than I said and the obstruction is one I had not seen. THE ALGEBRA WORKS, AND THE SAVING COMES FROM REUSING AN EXISTING CONSTRAINT. Our Slope2 already computes the halo2 quantity: its Spec asserts w*(xSe - rx) = 2*ry, i.e. 2y = w*(x_S - x). Stop treating that as the equation that DETERMINES w and treat it as the DEFINITION of y, and y/y' stop being witnesses. Four witnesses (lam1, x_S, w, x') and four constraints: (1) lam1*(t_x - x) = t_y - w*(x_S - x)/2; (2) x_S = lam1^2 - x - t_x; (3) x' = A^2 - x_S - x with A = lam1 + w free affine; (4) HANDOFF w'*(x_S' - x') + w*(x_S - x) = 2*A*(x' - x), which is the old y' = A(x'-x) - y with BOTH y's substituted — step i's from its own (w, x_S), step i+1's from ITS own (w', x_S'). Constraint (4) needs ZERO extra convolutions: its own is A*(x'-x), w*(x_S-x) is reused free from (1), and w'*(x_S'-x') free from step i+1. THE T-FORM PORT OF THE FIXED-BASE SIBLING IS THE WRONG DESIGN AND IS NEARLY WORTHLESS: anchoring the implied y to the last table point (y = lam*(u-x) - v) needs a FIFTH witness lam' — the chord slope of 2R and T — with its own certificate, giving 5 FRESH + 5 CERT + 2 convolutions = 2214/2239, a saving of only 84 per step.

x-ONLY ARITHMETIC: MY EARLIER COSTING WAS 2.5x TOO PESSIMISTIC, BUT THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES. I previously wrote that a Brier-Joye x-only ladder is '~10 field muls per bit ~ 2560 modmuls ~ 1.9M rows'. THE CORRECT FORMULAS ARE ONE DEGREE-4 CONGRUENCE PER GROUP OPERATION, both VERIFIED 200/200 on secp256k1: xADD is x+ * x- * (x1 - x2)^2 = (x1*x2)^2 - 28*(x1 + x2), and xDBL is 4*x'*(x^3 + 7) = x^4 - 56*x. These are Vieta applied to Semaev's third summation polynomial, which for b = 7 symmetrises to the 9-monomial e2^2 - 4*e1*e3 - 28*e1 = 0 (also verified 200/200). At 8x32 a D=4 certificate is 1004, so an x-only group operation is 512 + 1004 = 1516 against 2 x 745 = 1490 for a y-free affine one — A WASH PER OPERATION. IT STILL LOSES BY ABOUT 4x OVERALL, and the reason is STRUCTURAL, NOT ARITHMETIC: x-only forces a LADDER (the difference must be pinned), which forbids windowing and forbids the 4-dimensional fake-GLV, so it costs ~512 operations against our 62 steps. Real total about 775k, not 1.9M. ALSO STATE THE DO-NOT-TRY CORRECTLY: secp256k1 having prime order rules out the MONTGOMERY MODEL, not x-only differential arithmetic, which exists on every short Weierstrass curve. S_4 (191 monomials, degree 12, ~11 units) and S_5 (degree 32) are dead; division polynomials psi_n are degree n^2; elliptic nets / EDS are 8 independent degree-4 congruences per bit, about 19x worse than our 1.25.
GLV: decompose k = k1 + k2*lambda (mod n) into two ~128-bit halves; the endomorphism psi(x,y)=(beta*x mod p, y) costs ~6 constraints; then k*P = k1*P + k2*psi(P) halves the number of doublings.

GLV-3 / higher-dimensional decomposition (eprint 2025/1151, 2025/933): split k into THREE ~85-bit sub-scalars using the endomorphism twice (k = k0 + k1*lambda + k2*lambda^2 mod n); ~85 doublings instead of ~128, run as a joint 3-MSM sharing every doubling. Fewer doublings = fewer non-native Fp ops.

Find SHORTEST decomposition vectors via integer lattice reduction or a half-extended Euclidean algorithm in the endomorphism ring (eprint 2025/933); secp256k1's small CM discriminant (D=-3, j=0) admits extra reductions (reported 22-53% proving-time drop vs prior SOTA).
Run the decomposed halves/thirds as a width-w windowed joint-MSM (double-then-add) sharing doublings — reference figure ~2176 constraints for the 2-MSM core.
Per scalar bit the naive cost is ~4 (point selects) + ~4 (adds) + ~2 (double); wNAF / signed-digit windows cut the number of ADDITIONS via longer zero runs.

PRIME-REDUCE for a FIXED prime (circom-ecdsa): do limb mul/add WITHOUT carries into a wide form (k=4 x 64-bit registers for 256-bit; a product spans ~10 registers), then collapse 10 registers back to 4 in ONE reduction (~1000 constraints) by subtracting PRECOMPUTED multiples of p — compile-time constants because p is fixed. DEFERRAL BUDGET: keep 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < 254 (native field bits); that inequality tells you exactly how many unreduced products you may accumulate before a carry/reduce pass is actually required — defer right up to it, not further.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce, ~2x fewer reductions): accumulate a*b +/- c*d in WIDE UNREDUCED limbs and reduce ONCE at the end. Affine EC formulas are exactly this shape — lambda = (y2-y1)*inv(x2-x1), x3 = lambda^2 - x1 - x2, y3 = lambda*(x1-x3) - y1 — so reduce once PER OUTPUT COORDINATE, never per intermediate product.

DEFINITIVE CLOSURE OF THE COORDINATE-SYSTEM QUESTION, WITH THE RIGHT REASON — MY EARLIER REASON WAS WRONG. I wrote that 'an inversion costs ~1 allocation + 1 constraint'. THAT IS FALSE HERE: in the emulated setting a hinted inverse must be certified by x*inv = 1 mod p, which is a FULL certificate at ~901. What is actually true is that an affine DIVISION lam = num/den is ONE certificate (den*lam = num), i.e. exactly one modular multiplication — so I = M = S = 1 reduction, and every result in the ECC literature since 1985 optimises the ratio I/M in [8, 100] and therefore RUNS BACKWARDS here. Re-costed by MATERIALISATIONS PER GROUP OPERATION, which is what the master cost law charges for: affine (x,y) add 3 / double 3 (the 3x^2 folds into the slope certificate); affine (x, lambda) 2; affine (x, lambda) with the degree-3 merge 1.5; Jacobian 7-9; projective-complete 9-10; Meloni co-Z >= 10. JACOBIAN IS 3.5x WORSE, and no amount of free raw products rescues it, because a Jacobian doubling is degree 4 in (X, Y, Z) and degree 4 already costs more than two materialisations. EFD shortw/jacobian-0 confirms: DBL 2M+5S = 7 reductions against affine 3, ADD 11M+5S = 16 against 3. ALSO CLOSED: Montgomery's simultaneous-inversion trick is 3m-2 reductions against m for m hinted inversions — STRICTLY WORSE FOR EVERY m >= 2, do not batch inversions.
Use INCOMPLETE / affine addition formulas (cheaper than complete-addition) where exceptional cases are ruled out by the decomposition, guarded by a soundness argument.

Precomputed-points-as-HINTS (eprint 2025/933): compute the scalar-mul result and per-step accumulator points OUTSIDE the circuit and pass them as witnesses; the circuit only CHECKS each group-law relation, which is cheaper than deriving points in-circuit. The prior R1CS baseline was ~9 constraints per scalar bit — beat that per bit.

AUDIT FOR OVER-ALLOCATION in the incomplete-add ladder (circom-ecdsa finding): only the first ~3 steps actually need the complete-addition guard, so accumulator/point arrays sized [bits] can be cut to [bits-3] and [3]. Allocations are HALF the cost metric here — sweep every witness array for entries that are never constrained or never read.

Non-native Fp: minimal-limb schoolbook mul + reduce with carry-save accumulation and top-bit-fold limb range checks; the flexible-limb EqViaCarries family (see reference/) may pack the equality check tighter.

THE EISENTRAEGER-LAUTER-MONTGOMERY RECASTING: COMPUTE [2]P + Q AS (P+Q)+P AND NEVER FORM y_R — 5 ROWS PER DOUBLE-AND-ADD STEP INSTEAD OF 7. Source: zcash/zcash issue #3924 ('Faster variable-base scalar multiplication in zk-SNARK circuits'), which claims 6 constraints/bit against a prior best of 8.5 with recoded scalars. WARNING, AND THIS IS WHY IT CANNOT BE COPIED VERBATIM: the equations in that issue are for a MONTGOMERY curve B*y^2 = x^3 + A*x^2 + x, and secp256k1 has PRIME ORDER so it has no Montgomery form at all (see the Montgomery-ladder do-not-try note). Only the RECASTING transfers. DERIVED AND VERIFIED HERE for short Weierstrass with a = 0: the point is that y_R of the intermediate R = P+Q is never needed, because lam2 = (y_R - y_P)/(x_R - x_P) simplifies to lam1 + lam2 = -2*y_P/(x_R - x_P). FIVE ROWS, five allocations: (1) (x_Q - x_P)*lam1 = y_Q - y_P; (2) lam1*lam1 = x_R + x_P + x_Q; (3) (x_R - x_P)*(lam1 + lam2) = -2*y_P; (4) lam2*lam2 = x_S + x_P + x_R; (5) (x_P - x_S)*lam2 = y_S + y_P. Against the naive route — double (x*x = xsq; (2y)*lam = 3*xsq + a; lam*lam = x2 + 2x; (x - x2)*lam = y2 + y, 4 rows) then add (3 rows) = 7 — that is 2 rows AND 2 allocations saved, i.e. 4 SCORE PER SCALAR BIT. VERIFIED: 39991/39991 exact matches against reference (P+Q)+P over a small curve with a = 0, every output on the curve. THE EXCEPTIONAL CASES ARE COMPLETELY CHARACTERIZED, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE GUARD CHEAP: exactly two rows can degenerate — row 1 when x_Q = x_P (i.e. Q = +-P), and row 3 when x_R = x_P, which happens IF AND ONLY IF Q = -2P (verified: every sampled degeneracy was exactly that). Nothing else can fail, so an exception guard needs those two tests and no more. HONEST RANKING AGAINST WHAT WE ALREADY HAVE: the halo2 'never witness y in the loop' note above is the STRONGER form — it carries (x_A, lam) and drops row 5 as well, so ELM is strictly an intermediate. Use ELM where a y-coordinate genuinely has to exist at that step (window boundaries, the final point), and halo2's ladder everywhere else.

SLOPE-ONLY TERMINAL ASSERTION — PROVING 2*A + T = O COSTS ONE SLOPE GADGET AND FOUR ROWS, NOT A DOUBLE-AND-ADD. When the last step of a scalar-mul or MSM only has to ASSERT that the accumulator chain closes to infinity, do not compute 2A+T and test the flag. Write S = A + T for the chord sum: the chord formula gives y_S = lambda*(x_A - x_S) - y_A, which collapses to -y_A exactly when x_S = x_A. So 2A + T = O <=> S = -A <=> x_S = x_A. A slope gadget already produces lambda and x_S = lambda^2 - x_A - x_T, so the whole assertion is ONE row A.isInf - T.isInf = 0 plus FOUR rows (1 - A.isInf)*(x_S[k] - x_A[k]) = 0. MEASURED (secp256k1 over BN254, 4 limbs x 64 bits): 1070 allocations / 1085 constraints, against 1792/1809 for double-then-cancel and 1783/1802 for assert-negated-sum — 722 allocations and 724 constraints saved, and being a pure assertion it materialises no output point. THE ONE SOUNDNESS OBLIGATION: the degenerate branch where x_T = x_A makes the slope gadget return the TANGENT, and you must show that branch cannot satisfy the assertion. For a = 0, b = 7 it forces lambda^2 = 3x together with 2*y*lambda = 3x^2, hence x^3 = -28 and y^2 = -21; -21 is a quadratic NON-RESIDUE mod p, proved by one kernel `decide` on a binary modPow at ZERO circuit rows. Re-derive the analogous non-residue before using this on another curve.

DO NOT ASSUME COMPLETE ADDITION IS EXPENSIVE — WITH LIMB-LEVEL MUXES IT IS 1.3% OF A STEP, AND THIS OVERTURNS THE USUAL ADVICE. The received wisdom (and my own earlier notes) says to use incomplete affine addition and discharge the exceptions by a soundness argument. MEASURED, THAT IS THE WRONG TRADE IN THIS COST MODEL: a FULLY COMPLETE fused double-add step is 2346 allocations / 2371 constraints, of which the entire exception apparatus is about 30 allocations — the other 97.9% is the five non-native certificates. The apparatus is two 9-cell point muxes (9/9 each) for A = O and T = -A, two 256-bit equality tests at 5/5, and one 2/2 opposite-y detector. THREE TRICKS MAKE IT THIS CHEAP. (1) 256-BIT EQUALITY IN 5 ROWS: pack limbs 0,1 into one native element and limbs 2,3 into another (each under 128 bits, safely below the native modulus), run two IsZeroField at 2/2, AND them with one row. DO NOT COMPARE LIMBWISE. (2) T = -A IN 2 ROWS USING ONE LIMB: witness inv of y_A[0] - y_T[0], set oppY <== yDiff*inv, assert yDiff*(sameX - oppY) = 0. Only the LOW LIMB is needed, because two finite points with equal x are equal or opposite and p is odd, so y != -y already differs in limb 0. (3) A BOOLEAN OR THAT COSTS ZERO: if one input IMPLIES the other (here T = O re-routes the intermediate x so sameX is forced to 1), the OR EQUALS the implied flag, and a downstream flag - other is a free affine expression instead of a witness plus a row. SO: reach for incomplete formulas only where a cheaper SPECIALISED gadget results — e.g. adding P to phi(P), where x_{phiP} != x_P is free from beta != 1 and x != 0, worth 63 allocations — and not to avoid completeness per se.

DEFERRED SUM-OF-EIGHT MOD-n CONGRUENCE IN 38 ALLOCATIONS / 44 CONSTRAINTS. The GLV scalar-side relation u1 + lambda*u2 + s*(v1 + lambda*v2) = 0 (mod n) decomposes into four mod-n products; DO NOT REDUCE THEIR SUM. Split each term by its sign into a positive and a negative bucket, bias the positive side by a constant 4n (free — n is a compile-time constant so 4n is a constant limb vector), witness a SINGLE quotient q, range-check it to THREE BITS (2 allocations / 3 constraints), and assert sum(positives) + 4n = sum(negatives) + q*n with ONE grouped-carry limb equality (35/41). TOTAL 38/44. Against reducing each partial sum mod n that is roughly a 4x saving on the tail of the decomposition proof, and it is why the whole scalar relation is 2932/2954 = 1.65% of a 355748-score circuit. THE BIAS CONSTANT IS THE DESIGN PARAMETER: choose it so every limb of the positive side stays non-negative and the quotient bound stays tiny — four signed terms each below n need 4n and give q < 8.

THE RECORD'S TOP-LEVEL SHAPE, FOR ORIENTATION (355748 = 176973 allocations + 178775 constraints, read from its own cost proofs). 4-dimensional FAKE GLV with the result WITNESSED, never computed: witness Q (9 cells, 0 constraints), validate it on-curve and canonical (1864/1895 — which ALSO emits the output bytes for free), witness four signed 64-bit coefficients (260 allocations) with booleanity (260 constraints), assert the mod-n scalar relation (2932/2954), build a 16-entry table of all subset sums of {+-P, +-phiP, +-Q, +-phiQ} (16881/17074), then run a 64-position 4-way interleaved MSM that ENDS IN AN ASSERTION that u1*P + u2*phiP + v1*Q + v2*phiQ = O (155027/156592). NO RECODING AT ALL — no NAF, no wNAF, no signed digits; plain binary magnitude with one sign bit per coefficient, and signs applied to the TABLE POINTS. Window width 1 per coefficient, interleaved 4-wide, so each position consumes a 4-bit nibble indexing the 16-entry table. THE LOOP IS 87.6% OF THE CIRCUIT and one step is 2481/2506 = VarLookup 135/135 (a 4-level mux tree of 15 9-cell point muxes) plus FusedStep 2346/2371. The coefficient bound 2^64 = n^(1/4) comes from a PIGEONHOLE argument, not a lattice algorithm: (2^64)^4 > n forces a collision, and the short-coefficient property is used in exactly one place — ruling out the u = v = 0 forgery.

WHY THE Y-FREE LOOP IS CURRENTLY UNSATISFIABLE, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS A DIFFERENT PROJECT. The invariant 2y = w*(x_S - x) defines y only when x_S != x. Slope2.main FORCES x_S = x whenever T = O — `let xSe <- Mux { selector := tIsInf, ifTrue := rx, ifFalse := xS }` — deliberately, to reach the tangent branch. AND T = O IS GENERIC, NOT ADVERSARIAL: GLVBuildTable.lean:124 proves `subsetPoint B 0 = .infinity`, i.e. TABLE ENTRY 0 IS THE POINT AT INFINITY, because the table is SUBSET sums with no recoding. Nibble 0000 selects it with probability 1/16 per position; over 62 interior steps the expected count is 3.9 and P(never) = (15/16)^62 = 1.8%. So on essentially every honest input the y-free system asserts 0 = 2y and THE CIRCUIT IS UNSATISFIABLE — a completeness failure, not a corner case. DROPPING THE CONSTRAINT INSTEAD IS A TOTAL SOUNDNESS BREAK: w unconstrained => A = lam1 + w unconstrained => x' unconstrained => the accumulator is steerable => the terminal `= O` assertion is free, and because fake-GLV WITNESSES Q the prover can engineer the collision at will. Halo2 is safe only because its base is fixed and public and its exclusion argument (Halo paper Thm 3 plus an integer index-shadow loop) runs over Z with one bounded scalar; our rank-4 lattice with witnessed Q and phiQ = lambda*Q admits no such argument. FOUR ESCAPES CHECKED, ALL CLOSED: (i) tangent from the implied y is w*w*(x_S-x) = 3x^2, DEGREE 3 — our interpolatedMul is a degree-2 convolution at 7 points with a 71-bit folded quotient, and a triple product needs 10 points and a ~512-bit quotient, dearer than the 531 saved; (ii) the T-form is non-degenerate at x_S = x but its tangent is still cubic in mu*lam*(u-x), and reducing it needs a witnessed pi = w*lam at 440/445 — exactly what was saved; (iii) a reciprocal state iota = 1/(2y) makes the tangent degree 2 but the CHORD cubic; (iv) an offset/blinding point making the table O-free needs Delta != -T_j for 16 adversarial T_j. THE PREREQUISITE IS THE ALL-ODD SIGNED-DIGIT RECODE (see the fixed-base sibling's free-recode entry, 0/0 cost) so that no nibble can select the identity. Sequence it that way — the recode is independently valuable and also unblocks incomplete addition in the table build. EVEN AFTER THE RECODE, S = +-R (i.e. T = -2R) still has to be excluded by an index argument that could not be constructed for adversarial Q. TREAT THAT, NOT THE ALGEBRA, AS THE REAL OPEN QUESTION.

CORRECTION TO THE CERTIFICATE COST ATOMS I HAVE BEEN QUOTING — EVERY FIGURE WAS +8/+8 TOO HIGH. Read from the record's own cost proofs (Cost.lean / CostW2.lean / FusedCost.lean), the true atoms are: FRESH (a fresh canonical Fe: 4 limb witnesses + validP) = 264/267 = 531 score; CERT (mulModFold / mulModFoldT, a target-supplied reduction INCLUDING its own convolution) = 176/178 = 354; an extra interpolatedMul folded into an existing certificate = 7/7; DivOrZeroF3's zero-handling overhead = 28/28. Therefore mulModSub2 = FRESH + CERT = 440/445 (I said 448/453), divOrZeroF3 = FRESH + CERT + 28/28 = 468/473 (I said 476/481), FoldTarget = 182/184 (I said 184/186), fusedStep = 2306/2331 (I said 2346/2371), glvStep = 2441/2466, glvMSMAssert = 153244/154813 (I said 155027/156592). The current step's certificate content is 2*468/473 + 3*440/445 = 2256/2281, i.e. 4537 of the step's 4637 = 97.8%. Y-FREE EXCEPTION LEDGER AND HANDOFF, MEASURED. WHICH DETECTORS SURVIVE: R = O is a flag, fine. T = R is sameX1 = [t_x = x] (EqFe 5/5, x-only) and ITS TANGENT BRANCH IS FIXABLE FOR FREE — on that branch y = t_y and t_y is materialised by the table lookup, so use 2*t_y as the tangent denominator and stay at degree 2. T = -R IS BROKEN: the 2/2 limb-0 trick (witness inv of y_A[0] - y_T[0]) has no analogue because y is never limb-decomposed, so there is no limb 0 to compare. The replacement is a sign bit c with a gated target-supplied certificate asserting w*(x_S - x) = (1 - 2c)*2*t_y under sameX1, ESTIMATED ~190/200 = 390 score per step against 4 today — that alone eats ~24,000 of the ~60,900 saving, and there is no precedent in the record for gating a grouped-carry identity by a boolean, so treat the number as soft. THE HANDOFF IS NOT A PROBLEM. The terminal GLVStepLastAssertLow (1767/1786) produces no y but CONSUMES y_A in its slope gadget; substituting y_A = w*(x_S - x)/2 from the last interior step costs +7/7 ONCE and reuses that step's convolution. Step 62's handoff has no step 63 to reference so it reverts to materialising y_63 at 440/445 — exactly Sinsemilla's selector-blended boundary gate — costing one step of 62. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: constraint (4) references w' and x_S', so EMIT IT AT THE TOP OF STEP i+1; the foldlRange state grows from FlaggedPoint (9 cells) to (x', x, lam1, w, x_S, isInf) (21 cells) and the two output point muxes go 9/9 -> 21/21, +24/+24 per step. FULL PREDICTED LEDGER against glvMSMAssertCost = 153244/154813, BEST CASE (exceptions EXCLUDED, i.e. recode landed AND the index argument found): 61 steps x (-489/-494) = -59,963; terminal substitution +14; wider fold state +2,976; non-degeneracy asserts +1,736; NET -55,237, loop ~125,778/127,042, circuit ~300,500 +- the GLVBuildTable / GLVScalarRelation signed-digit rework (bracket -2,000 to +3,000). IF EXCEPTIONS MUST STAY ROUTED the saving collapses to ~98 per step while the rebuilt oppY costs ~390 per step: NET ABOUT +18,000, STRICTLY WORSE THAN TODAY.

THE MASTER COST LAW, DERIVED FROM THE RECORD'S OWN GADGETS AND CALIBRATED TO 1.6%: score ~= 2 * M * (256 + Wq + Wc), where M is THE NUMBER OF MATERIALISED EMULATED FIELD ELEMENTS. The multiply-subtract decomposes EXACTLY as 512 + 19 + 370: 512 = 4 limbs x (63 alloc + 64 constr) of ToBitsAffine plus 4 witness allocs = materialising ONE element; 19 = the sparse x

= 256 rows; the record's 252 allocations + 256 constraints is EXACTLY that floor. CONSEQUENCE THAT REFRAMES THE WHOLE PROBLEM: no encoding trick makes a 256-bit range check cheaper, so the ONLY lever on the 86% of the circuit that is range-check bits is REDUCING M. 'Carry values unreduced for several steps' is NOT the answer; 'never let the intermediate exist' is.

*** PARTIALLY RETRACTED — READ THE 'ALL-ODD RECODE DOES NOT MAKE THE TABLE IDENTITY-FREE' ENTRY BEFORE ACTING ON THIS ONE. Its instruction 'SHIP THE TWO TOGETHER OR NEITHER' IS WRONG (the lookup arithmetic is off by 30 per lookup and 8x32 alone is still worth about -32.4k, so SHIP 8x32 ALONE), and its CERT figures 365 -> 214 and '-26,600 over 62 steps' are mutually inconsistent (151/cert against 86/cert); the measured pair is CERT(4x64) = 354 and CERT(8x32) ~ 205. The limb-alignment INSIGHT below is correct and is why the lever works at all — keep it, ignore the numbers and the shipping instruction. *** THE FOLD CONSTANT'S LIMB ALIGNMENT IS WORTH 22 BITS OF CARRY, AND IT IS THE GATE ON EVERYTHING ELSE. c = 2^32 + 977 is ONE 33-bit limb in base 2^64 (f = 32) but the two TINY limbs (977, 1) in base 2^32 (f ~ 10) — and f enters the carry width LINEARLY. Re-costing the certificate post-fold with the master law: 4x64 CERT = 365, 8x32 CERT = 214, 9x29 = 218, 10x26 = 213, 16x16 = 186. The gain splits as -64 bits from n and -44 from f, against +16 for the extra cells. THE PENALTY IS THE MUX, NOT THE CERTIFICATE: VarLookup is 15 FlaggedPoint muxes of 2k+1 cells, so 135 rows at k=4 and 255 at k=8 (+240 per step, +14,880 over the loop) — WHICH IS EXACTLY CANCELLED by porting the fixed-base all-odd recode (an 8-entry +- table is 7 nodes x 2k cells + k negate rows = 120 rows at k=8). SHIP THE TWO TOGETHER OR NEITHER. Modelled effect of 8x32 alone: -26,600 over 62 steps plus about -6,000 on the ~40 non-loop certificates. THIS CORROBORATES THE OLD 26-32-BIT CROSS-CODEBASE FINDING FROM A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT DIRECTION, POST-FOLD: 901 -> ~745 per multiply-subtract is 17%, against the 18-22% the pre-fold comparison predicted. NON-UNIFORM LIMBS DO NOT HELP: cell magnitude is driven by the MAXIMUM limb width, so [32,64,64,64,32] still gives 2^130 cells and buys nothing; the RSA MixedRadix gadget does not transfer, and no constraint system in existence uses non-uniform limbs.

DEGREE-3 CERTIFICATES: PUT A POLYNOMIAL IN A *FACTOR*, NOT ONLY IN THE TARGET, AND DELETE A WHOLE MATERIALISATION. The corpus already keeps a raw convolution as a certificate TARGET (free). The new move is to keep one as a FACTOR, which costs one extra fold level and is affordable ONLY once f is small. MEASURED IN THE MODEL: CERT(D=3) is 1597 at 4x64 — the folded position exceeds 2^253, INFEASIBLE, the group check cannot pack even one position — but 454 at 8x32. Since a materialisation is 531, the merge gain is -700 (A LOSS) at 4x64 and +290 at 8x32. PORT THE FIXED-BASE ALL-ODD RECODE INTO THE VARIABLE-BASE LOOP — IT HALVES THE TABLE, HALVES THE LOOKUP, AND DELETES THE EXCEPTION APPARATUS. Recode each 64-bit fake-GLV coefficient with digits d_i = 2*b_i - 1 in {+-1} (a pure wire permutation, 0/0), so sum d_i 2^i = 2m - 2^64 + 1 and EVERY DIGIT IS NONZERO. Then no position can select the identity and no two consecutive sites can collide, so the whole loop uses INCOMPLETE addition guarded by a Lean hypothesis: -100 per step of exception apparatus. The table becomes 8 entries (+- pairs) instead of 16, so VarLookup goes from 15 muxes of 9 cells to 7 muxes of 8 cells plus a k-row conditional y-negation: 135 -> 60 rows at k=4, 255 -> 120 at k=8. THE PARITY OBLIGATION AND ITS HONEST PRICE: the fake-GLV kernel lattice has determinant n, which is ODD, so it surjects onto (Z/2)^4 and an all-odd representative ALWAYS exists — but the pigeonhole bound then needs |u| < 2^65..2^66, i.e. ONE OR TWO EXTRA LOOP STEPS (+3k to +6k) against ~22k saved. CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE IF THAT IS UNPALATABLE: offset every table entry by a fixed constant point C; the accumulated (2^64 - 1)*C is a compile-time constant, so the terminal assertion becomes sum = (2^64 - 1)*C at ZERO cost — though that only kills the identity case, not consecutive collisions. NOTE THIS IS ALSO THE PREREQUISITE FOR THE Y-FREE LOOP, which is blocked precisely because table entry 0 is the point at infinity.

THE j=0 CM IDENTITY P + phi(P) = (beta^2 * x, -y) COSTS ZERO ROWS — CORRECTING MY OWN 'j-INVARIANT 0 BUYS NOTHING' NOTE. Because 1 + lambda + lambda^2 = 0 in the endomorphism ring, P, phi(P) and phi^2(P) are COLLINEAR (they are the three intersections of the horizontal line y = y_P with y^2 = x^3 + 7), so P + phi(P) = -phi^2(P) = (beta^2 * x_P, -y_P) — a pure constant scaling and a negation, BOTH FREE. VERIFIED 200/200 on real secp256k1 points. The 16-entry fake-GLV table needs 11 non-trivial subset sums of {P, phiP, Q, phiQ}; two of them (P + phiP and Q + phiQ) are now free, so the build drops from about 12.6 additions to 9, worth roughly -5,400. MY EARLIER NOTE SAID 'j-invariant 0 / a = 0 buys exactly zero rows' — that is true of the ENDOMORPHISM EVALUATION (a field addition is free), but the COLLINEARITY relation is a genuine free group addition and the corpus was not using it.

FAKE GLV CANNOT GO PAST DIMENSION 4, AND THE REASON IS SOUNDNESS, NOT COST. I previously recorded only that 6-dim measured 70% worse. The sharper fact: adding a THIRD witnessed point R with a prover-chosen multiple makes the kernel lattice rank 6 with coefficients ~n^(1/6) ~ 2^43, but the relation u1*P + u2*phiP + v1*Q + v2*phiQ + w1*R + w2*phiR = O is SATISFIABLE FOR ANY Q by choosing R appropriately — the verifier can only check the mod-n scalar congruence for the KNOWN scalars, so R is unconstrained and soundness collapses outright. Genuine 8-dimensional GLV needs a GLS curve over F_p^2. 64 POSITIONS IS THE FLOOR FOR THIS FAMILY; stop sweeping the dimension. RELATEDLY, DETERMINISTIC BATCHING OF THE PER-STEP CONGRUENCES IS CLOSED BOTH WAYS: asserting sum_i 2^(s*i) * D_i = 0 over the integers IS sound (radix uniqueness pins each D_i = 0 given |D_i| < 2^(s-1)) — but it SAVES NOTHING, because the grouped-carry cost is linear in the number of limb POSITIONS and stacking three certificates triples the positions. Schul-Ganz & Segev, 'Accumulators in (and Beyond) Generic Groups: Non-Trivial Batch Verification Requires Interaction', TCC 2020 / eprint 2020/1106, prove the general statement. THE ONE TECHNIQUE THAT DOES BEAT RECOMPUTATION for Q = [k]P is Eagen's ECIP (eprint 2022/596, ~100x fewer multiplications via principal divisors and Weil reciprocity) and it buys that saving PRECISELY by evaluating at a random point — so it is the single escape hatch if the no-challenge constraint ever relaxes, and nothing else in the ECDLP, index-calculus, EDS or VDF literature is deterministic.

secp256k1-fixed-base-scalar-mul: HEAD-TO-HEAD MODMUL COUNTS ACROSS FOUR CODEBASES, ALL COMPILED AND MEASURED IN OUR MODEL (no lookups, no challenges), for one 256-bit a*b mod p over BN254: jsnark/xJsnark with a CONSTANT modulus and lazy range = 623 constraints at 32-bit chunks; jsnark with a variable modulus = 637 at 26-bit; arkworks r1cs-std emulated_fp = 680 (66 for mul_without_reduce + 614 for reduce) at 17 limbs x 15 bits; gnark v0.8.1 = 724 at 26x10 and 888 at its shipped 64x4. LIMB WIDTH 26-32 IS OPTIMAL AND 64 IS 18-22% WORSE — measured independently in two different codebases, and it reproduces xJsnark's own Figure 5 parameter sweep (b about 32 near-optimal, b = 120 about 40% worse). WE USE 4 LIMBS OF 64 BITS, i.e. the worst end of that curve; this is the same conclusion the pseudo-Mersenne analysis reached from a different direction, so treat 32-bit limbs as strongly corroborated. STRUCTURE OF THE COST, which is why: product limbs hinted and verified at 2n-1 FIXED points costs 2n-1 rows (15 at w=32) and is essentially free; q*p is FREE when p is a compile-time constant since constant scalings are linear; grouped carry propagation is 60-110; and ABOUT 80% OF THE WHOLE THING is bit-decomposition range checks on the quotient and remainder. LAZY REDUCTION IS WORTH ABOUT 600 CONSTRAINTS PER AVOIDED REDUCE (arkworks measures mul_without_reduce at 66 against reduce at 614, and additions cost literally zero), so a*b + c*d with one shared reduction is about 746 against 1360. FINALLY, WHY GNARK'S HEADLINE 99 CONSTRAINTS PER EMULATED MUL IS NOT AVAILABLE: modern gnark's mulMod emits ZERO constraints and defers to a Schwartz-Zippel check at a commitment-derived challenge (std/math/emulated/field_mul.go), and std/multicommit panics outright if the frontend is not a Committer — so it cannot even compile on a plain Groth16 frontend. Strip the challenge and the lookups and gnark's own pre-v0.10 code lands at 724.

MEASURED TARGET FOR THE MODMUL: 845 SCORE, AGAINST OUR 1463 (mulModSub2Cost = 728 alloc + 735 constr). These numbers come from actually compiling circuits with circom 2.2.3 and reading row counts out of the .r1cs with snarkjs, then witness-testing on 508 vectors including the worst case (p-1)^2 — not from a paper. Reference points, as rows + allocations: circom-ecdsa BigMultModP(64,4) = 7707; circom-pairing FpMultiply(43,6) at secp256k1 = 2509; fold with tightened carry parameters at n=32,k=8 = 1527; FOLD + CRT at n=32,k=8 = 845 (424 rows + 421 allocs). THREE INGREDIENTS, IN ORDER OF IMPORTANCE. (1) THE PRODUCT IS ALREADY FREE — the full 256x256 limb product is 2k-1 rows by asserting the limb-polynomial identity at 2k-1 evaluation points (circom-ecdsa's BigMultNoCarry is 7 rows), so 99.8% of a naive BigMultModP is carries and range checks and NO effort should go into the multiplication. (2) THE FOLD IS FREE FOR EVERY MODULUS — reducing the 2k-1 product limbs back to k via precomputed constants 2^(n(k+i)) mod p is a LINEAR COMBINATION, zero rows. What p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977 buys is that the fold coefficients are TINY (literally 977 and 1 when n = 32, because c = 2^32 + 977 is limb-aligned there), which cascades: folded limb width 77 bits instead of 101, quotient bound 36 bits instead of 68, CRT limbs 2 instead of 3, carry width 46 instead of 70 — worth about 27% (424 vs 578 rows for a generic 256-bit prime, both compiled). USE n = 32 PRECISELY BECAUSE c IS LIMB-ALIGNED THERE. (3) THE BIG ONE — CHECK THE IDENTITY BY CRT, NOT BY A CARRY CHAIN (Lubarov and Baylina, 'Casting out Primes', eprint 2022/1470): verify under a FIXED set of moduli M = {r_BN254, 2^(nT)} and conclude the identity holds mod lcm(M), which suffices when |f| < lcm(M). NOTE THIS NEEDS NO RANDOM CHALLENGE — the moduli are fixed constants, so it maps to plain R1CS. Mod r_BN254 the check R - p*X - out = 0 is ONE PURELY LINEAR ROW because the modulus is a CONSTANT; mod 2^(nT) only T = 2 carries at 46 bits are needed instead of a full chain of 8. Soundness margin measured at 25 bits (|D|max = 2^293 < r*2^64 = 2^318) and brute-forced on scaled-down analogues. CAVEAT FOR RSA: there the modulus is an INPUT, so p*X is a genuine product and the native leg is NOT free — this transfers to the secp challenges much better than to RSA.

LAZY REDUCTION IS WORTH FAR MORE THAN IT LOOKS, BECAUSE LIMB PRODUCTS ADD FOR FREE. Measured, same compiled setup: sharing ONE reduction across M products costs 424 rows at M=1, 457 at M=2, 490 at M=4, 553 at M=8 — i.e. 424, 228, 123 and 69 rows PER MULTIPLICATION. Each extra product adds only about 15 rows (the 2k-1 convolution) plus roughly one bit to the carry widths, verified correct including at M*(p-1)^2. Affine EC formulas ARE sums of products. CORRECTION TO THE CANONICALITY FIGURE IN THIS ENTRY: I claimed the pseudo-Mersenne shape gives x < p in 37 rows against 333 for a generic comparison. THE SELECTOR IS 20.5% OF THE CIRCUIT, NOT ~2% — MY EARLIER NOTE HAD BOTH THE GADGET AND ITS MULTIPLICITY WRONG. It costed SelectX.mainX at 342 and said 'x2'. THE ONE-HOT BOUND (minimum 2^w - w - 1 multiplications to build a full one-hot from w bits, split-invariant) IS NOT CONTRADICTED — the record never builds a 2^11 one-hot at all, it factors it (see the factored-one-hot entry). WHERE THE BOUND NOW BINDS, AND A FREE 420 SCORE: the outer 4-bit one-hot HITS the bound at 2 + 9 = 11 = 2^4 - 4 - 1 exactly. The inner 7-bit half misses it by exactly 10 — the record pays blk 3 + inner4 15 + inner6 48 + inner7 64 = 130 against the optimum 3 + 9 + 45 + 63 = 120 = 2^7 - 7 - 1. The fix is mechanical and the construction is ALREADY PRESENT in the same file (hot4o's 'drop the last row AND the last column' identity): inner4 should witness 9 not 15 (cell(i,3) = a_i - sum_j h[i+3j], cell(3,j) = c_j - sum_i h[3j+i], cell(3,3) from the two); inner6 should be 45 not 48 (drop the last row too, recoverable from sum_a hot6(a,c) = pair2(c)); inner7 should be 63 not 64 (sum_a hot7(a,1) = xExpr(6)). 10 allocations + 10 constraints per window x 21 windows = 420 score. THE OTHER LEVER IS STILL OPEN: selecting a one-wire borrow instead of a whole 4-limb p-y array drops the output-wire count from 12 to 9, which by the factored formula gives 120 + 11 + 135 + 15 = 281 per window.

VERIFICATION TIME IS A HARD CONSTRAINT, NOT JUST COST (observed, twice). A solution scoring 80191 — beating the 80195 record, no sorry/admit, all required declarations present, cost parsed clean — was submitted and came back status=timeout from the zk.golf verifier. It was re-downloaded from the job and submitted a SECOND time and timed out identically, so this is a property of the solution, not a transient. It differs from the verified 80195 in 20 files (Chain, PairAdd, AffineChainAdd, CheapIncompleteAdd, FinalAdd), i.e. a real structural rework, at the same file count (148) and the same maxHeartbeats profile. LESSON: a lower-cost solution that cannot be CHECKED inside the verifier's budget scores nothing. Keep elaboration cheap as you golf — prefer many small lemmas over one huge `decide`/`simp` blowup, avoid raising maxHeartbeats to paper over a slow proof, and if a rewrite makes the build dramatically slower, treat that as a cost regression even though it does not show up in allocations+constraints.

SUPERSEDED — KEEP ONLY AS BACKGROUND. The halo2 fixed-base trick of offsetting window w's table by a constant so no window can select the identity is real, but the all-odd signed-digit recode (see the free-recode entry) achieves the same guarantee AND halves every table AND needs no last-window correction term. Use the recode, not the offset.

Base G is FIXED: every window multiple j*(2^{w*i})*G is a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT — bake the whole comb table into the circuit as constants (zero constraints to build it), unlike the variable-base case.
Comb method: k = sum b_{i} 2^{i}; group bits into d combs of width w so each step is ONE table select + ONE add; fewer adds than plain windowed double-and-add.
Width-w NAF / signed-digit recoding of the scalar so table entries cover +/- multiples, halving table size and generating more zero (skip) positions.

Signed-digit tables cost almost nothing to apply: -P = (x, -y), so the sign bit drives ONE modular negation of y (an affine op), NOT a second multiplexer. So a width-w signed table needs only 2^{w-1} constant entries selected, plus a conditional y-negation — half the select cost of an unsigned width-w table for the same window count.
Constant-table point selection as a multiplexer over field constants: select cost is linear in window size but touches only additions/booleans, no non-native mul.

PRIME-REDUCE for a FIXED prime (circom-ecdsa): do limb mul/add WITHOUT carries into a wide form (k=4 x 64-bit registers for 256-bit; a product spans ~10 registers), then collapse 10 registers back to 4 in ONE reduction (~1000 constraints) by subtracting PRECOMPUTED multiples of p — compile-time constants because p is fixed. DEFERRAL BUDGET: keep 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < 254 (native field bits); that inequality tells you exactly how many unreduced products you may accumulate before a carry/reduce pass is actually required — defer right up to it, not further.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce, ~2x fewer reductions): accumulate a*b +/- c*d in WIDE UNREDUCED limbs and reduce ONCE at the end. Affine EC formulas are exactly this shape — lambda = (y2-y1)*inv(x2-x1), x3 = lambda^2 - x1 - x2, y3 = lambda*(x1-x3) - y1 — so reduce once PER OUTPUT COORDINATE, never per intermediate product.

COORDINATE-SYSTEM TRAP: in R1CS an inversion costs ~1 allocation + 1 constraint (hint inv as a witness, enforce x*inv = 1), so division is nearly FREE here — the opposite of the software cost model. Jacobian/projective/co-Z formulas (incl. Meloni co-Z ladders at ~11M+5S+23A per scalar bit) exist ONLY to avoid inversion, and pay for it with extra MULTIPLICATIONS — which are the expensive non-native op in-circuit. Prefer plain AFFINE add/double with hinted inverses; do NOT port inversion-free coordinate systems from the ECC literature.

Combine comb sub-scalars as a joint accumulation sharing point doublings/additions (multi-comb), analogous to the joint-MSM trick, so the fixed precompute is amortized across all windows in one add-chain.

Port secp256k1-scalar-mul's GroupedEqXV / MulModTarget non-native machinery (see reference/) if it lowers the per-add Fp mul-mod cost below the current Flex path; competitor csko pushed this challenge to 90041, a large structural gap — a comb-table + incomplete-add rewrite is likely needed, not incremental tweaks.

GLV BUYS NOTHING ON A FIXED-BASE COMB — MY EARLIER ENTRY CLAIMING IT IS 'STRICTLY BETTER AND MISSING FROM THIS PLAYBOOK' IS WRONG, DO NOT SPEND A SLOT ON IT. GLV halves the number of DOUBLINGS. A comb has NO in-circuit doublings at all — the doubling ladder is a table of compile-time constants — so the in-circuit work is exactly ONE table select plus ONE addition PER WINDOW, and the window count is (scalar bits)/w regardless of how the scalar is split. Concretely: today 21 windows of 12 bits covers 252 bits; with k = k1 + k2*lambda you get 2 x ceil(128/12) = 22 windows, i.e. MORE additions, plus a mod-n decomposition check (~3000 by analogy with the variable-base ScalarRelation at 2932/2954). The same argument kills GLV-3 and 4-dimensional splitting here, and it is why mLSB-set comb + GLV is a SOFTWARE win (it shrinks the precomputed table, which is FREE for us) and not a circuit win. THE ONLY LEVERS THAT ACTUALLY MOVE A COMB ARE: fewer windows (wider w, bounded by the chord-slope table's elaboration cost), a cheaper selector, and a cheaper per-addition certificate.

Push the same idea further: with all tables being compile-time constants there is no table-size penalty for HIGHER-DIMENSIONAL decomposition (GLV-3 via lambda^2, or 4-dimensional GLV). Each extra dimension shortens the sub-scalars (256 -> ~128 -> ~85 -> ~64 bits) and shortens the shared doubling chain proportionally, at the cost only of more CONSTANT tables (free) and a slightly bigger decomposition check. Sweep the dimension and pick the minimum of (doublings + selects + decomposition check).

mLSB-set comb is the standard pairing of comb methods with GLV curves (see the fixed-base comb / GLV-GLS literature) — combine mLSB-set recoding with the two (or more) constant tables rather than treating comb and GLV as alternatives.

SLOPE-ONLY TERMINAL ASSERTION — PROVING 2*A + T = O COSTS ONE SLOPE GADGET AND FOUR ROWS, NOT A DOUBLE-AND-ADD. When the last step of a scalar-mul or MSM only has to ASSERT that the accumulator chain closes to infinity, do not compute 2A+T and test the flag. Write S = A + T for the chord sum: the chord formula gives y_S = lambda*(x_A - x_S) - y_A, which collapses to -y_A exactly when x_S = x_A. So 2A + T = O <=> S = -A <=> x_S = x_A. A slope gadget already produces lambda and x_S = lambda^2 - x_A - x_T, so the whole assertion is ONE row A.isInf - T.isInf = 0 plus FOUR rows (1 - A.isInf)*(x_S[k] - x_A[k]) = 0. MEASURED (secp256k1 over BN254, 4 limbs x 64 bits): 1070 allocations / 1085 constraints, against 1792/1809 for double-then-cancel and 1783/1802 for assert-negated-sum — 722 allocations and 724 constraints saved, and being a pure assertion it materialises no output point. THE ONE SOUNDNESS OBLIGATION: the degenerate branch where x_T = x_A makes the slope gadget return the TANGENT, and you must show that branch cannot satisfy the assertion. For a = 0, b = 7 it forces lambda^2 = 3x together with 2*y*lambda = 3x^2, hence x^3 = -28 and y^2 = -21; -21 is a quadratic NON-RESIDUE mod p, proved by one kernel `decide` on a binary modPow at ZERO circuit rows. Re-derive the analogous non-residue before using this on another curve.

DO NOT ASSUME COMPLETE ADDITION IS EXPENSIVE — WITH LIMB-LEVEL MUXES IT IS 1.3% OF A STEP, AND THIS OVERTURNS THE USUAL ADVICE. The received wisdom (and my own earlier notes) says to use incomplete affine addition and discharge the exceptions by a soundness argument. MEASURED, THAT IS THE WRONG TRADE IN THIS COST MODEL: a FULLY COMPLETE fused double-add step is 2346 allocations / 2371 constraints, of which the entire exception apparatus is about 30 allocations — the other 97.9% is the five non-native certificates. The apparatus is two 9-cell point muxes (9/9 each) for A = O and T = -A, two 256-bit equality tests at 5/5, and one 2/2 opposite-y detector. THREE TRICKS MAKE IT THIS CHEAP. (1) 256-BIT EQUALITY IN 5 ROWS: pack limbs 0,1 into one native element and limbs 2,3 into another (each under 128 bits, safely below the native modulus), run two IsZeroField at 2/2, AND them with one row. DO NOT COMPARE LIMBWISE. (2) T = -A IN 2 ROWS USING ONE LIMB: witness inv of y_A[0] - y_T[0], set oppY <== yDiff*inv, assert yDiff*(sameX - oppY) = 0. Only the LOW LIMB is needed, because two finite points with equal x are equal or opposite and p is odd, so y != -y already differs in limb 0. (3) A BOOLEAN OR THAT COSTS ZERO: if one input IMPLIES the other (here T = O re-routes the intermediate x so sameX is forced to 1), the OR EQUALS the implied flag, and a downstream flag - other is a free affine expression instead of a witness plus a row. SO: reach for incomplete formulas only where a cheaper SPECIALISED gadget results — e.g. adding P to phi(P), where x_{phiP} != x_P is free from beta != 1 and x != 0, worth 63 allocations — and not to avoid completeness per se.

THE ALL-ODD SIGNED-DIGIT RECODE COSTS EXACTLY ZERO ROWS, AND THE SCALAR'S PARITY IS ABSORBED BY THE TOP WINDOW'S CONSTANT TABLE. Do not build a recoder. With MSB-first input bits, define db[c] := bits[254 - c] for c < 255 and db[255] := 1 — a pure WIRE PERMUTATION with one hard-coded 1, cost 0/0. Grouping db into W windows of w bits gives digits d_i = 2*v_i + 1 - 2^w, all ODD and in +-{1, 3, ..., 2^w - 1}, and the identity sum_i d_i * 2^(w*i) = k + 1 - bits[255] holds. THE PARITY FIX IS FREE: the comb computes k*G when the scalar is odd and (k+1)*G when even, and the -+G correction is folded into the TOP window's table by making the scalar's LSB an extra INDEX BIT of that table — a 16-entry 4-bit top table costs 11 rows whether or not the parity bit is in the index, so the fix costs NOTHING. WHAT THIS BUYS, AND IT IS THE WHOLE EXCEPTION STORY: every digit is odd hence nonzero, so no window can ever select the identity, and no two consecutive sites can collide — which is what lets the entire ladder use incomplete addition with no runtime guard except the 44-score final screen. SECOND BENEFIT: the magnitude index of a NEGATIVE digit is the bitwise COMPLEMENT of the magnitude bits, obtained as XNOR(sign, b_i) at ONE multiplication per bit (11 for w = 12), so the sign costs 11 rows and no separate table.

A 43000-ENTRY CONSTANT POINT TABLE IS PROVABLE IN LEAN ONLY VIA CHORD-SLOPE CHAINS — BUDGET THIS BEFORE WIDENING THE WINDOW. If you widen the window the blocker is not circuit cost but ELABORATION: proving T[win][j] = (2j+1)*2^(w*win)*G for 21 x 2048 entries by group-law evaluation will not finish. The record instead stores, PER WINDOW, a list of 2047 precomputed CHORD SLOPES (21 x 2047 = 43248 hex constants) and certifies each whole window with ONE chordChainOK application, so each entry's certificate is a cheap field identity (y_{j+1} - y_j) = s_j*(x_{j+1} - x_j) rather than a group-law computation. The doubling ladder between windows is a separate 256-entry slope table. SCALING: w = 13 needs 19 x 4095 = about 78k slope constants and w = 14 needs 18 x 8191 = about 147k. REMEMBER THE VERIFIER TIMEOUT — a table this size stresses it directly, and a timeout is reported as a FAILURE, not as a bad score.

WIDE-FOLD BOUND DERIVATION, DONE AND GREEN ON ALL FOUR SITES — THE LEVER IS UNBLOCKED. The fold's carry width is set by exactly ONE clause of GVXHyps: (a) OFF_R(k) + OFF_L(k) < 2^(W k), and OFF_L(0) = cFold*C/2^64 = C/2^32 where C is the max convolution coefficient at a position. Everything else — the field-capacity clauses (d) and the final-group clause — has 2^23 or more of headroom at every site and NEVER BINDS. GroupedFlex cost = (sum_{k<G-2}(W_k - 1), sum_{k<G-2} W_k + 1); the fold's L=5, gf=2, G=3 layout is FORCED (gf=3 pushes Sigma_L to 2^290 > r), so there is no schedule search to do.
